docs.x: Open the practice model from the start screen. Launch PetaNuri3D. Click Try the sample in the middle. When "Shinobu" appears in the middle, you're ready. The first time you launch, a guided tour (Tutorial) appears. You can follow it, or close it with "Skip" or Esc and continue on this page. Shinobu is divided by body part into texture sets (the unit of one texture). The app automatically switches to the set where you start drawing, so you don't need to worry about it now. That part's texture set is selected and briefly lights up with a soft color. Press Ctrl+Shift+N. The leftmost button at the bottom of the Layers panel does the same. docs.x: PetaNuri3D has two operations: "Save", which keeps your work, and "Export", which creates the texture images. Press Ctrl+S to save to a project file (.petanuri). You can't find the panel you want, or the layout is messed up: Open the panel from Display → Windows, or reset the layout (Panel list, Reset the layout). Transparent areas look gray or checkered, or low-resolution textures look blurry: These are display settings (How light and transparency look). docs.h: Can't paint, or paint doesn't land where you want
docs.x: Strokes leave no color, or only part of the area paints: The cause is a hidden or locked layer, a selection left over, or similar (Draw your first stroke). You can't paint outside a selection, or can't paint where you want: A selection is still active. Deselect it, then paint (Selection). Painting doesn't change the picture: You're set to draw on the layer mask (Layer mask). Whatever color you pick, it only paints gray: You're still painting a paint target (shadow color, a mask and so on). Click "Back to color" to return (Paint target). You can't add a layer (Lite): Lite allows up to 4 layers per texture set, including the base (Layers). Painting jumps to another texture set: This is the function that switches automatically to the set where you start drawing. You can turn it off (Choose the set to draw on). You can't paint over another texture set, or lines break at the neck seam: Check the setting for painting across two sets (Paint across two sets, When you can't paint). You can't paint under clothes or inside hair: Hide the faces in front and you can paint what's behind (Visible area, Hide pen). Part of the model stays hidden: You hid it. Press Alt+H to show everything again. Hiding isn't recorded in Undo (Visible area). Paint also lands on the opposite side of a thick part: "Also paint back and hidden faces" is on (Also paint back and hidden faces). You can't paint in Pose mode: See Pose mode.

docs.x: Double-click setup.exe in the "PetaNuri3D" folder. Choose where to install, whether to add a desktop icon, and whether double-clicking a project file (.petanuri) opens it. You don't need administrator rights (it installs for your user only). Launch it from the Start menu (or the desktop). setup.exe installs the app from the same folder. Don't take setup.exe out on its own; use the whole folder. It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\PetaNuri3D.

Put the "PetaNuri3D" folder anywhere you like. Double-click PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe in the folder. The app also uses resources.neu, mcp, tools and unity next to the exe. When you move it, move the whole folder. Extract a new version into a new folder.

You're ready when "New", "Open project file" and "Try the sample" appear in the middle. You can also open recent files and autosaves from here. You can also start by dropping a 3D model (FBX etc.) or a project file (.petanuri) onto the entrance in the middle of the startup screen. A 3D model goes on to the New screen; a project file opens right away. Your settings (sub tools, key bindings, window layout, color sets, reference images and so on) are saved in %APPDATA%\PetaNuri3D and come back the next time you launch. To remove the app, uninstall "PetaNuri3D" in Windows "Settings → Apps → Installed apps". Your settings and project files aren't deleted.

"Windows protected your PC" appears: Click "More info", then "Run anyway". The app isn't code-signed, so this can appear the first time. Unity link stops working after you moved the app: Select the exe location again, once, in the Unity add-on, which remembers where the exe is (Paint from Unity).

The first time you launch, a guided tour (tutorial) appears. You follow it by actually touching the highlighted spots. Use ← → to go back and forward. To quit, choose "Skip" or press Esc. When no model is open, you can choose "Try with the sample model" or "With my own model (open later)". With the sample, you can try rotating, drawing, symmetry and UV in turn. To see it again, choose Help → "Tutorial (guided tour)". You can also turn it on with File → Preferences → System, "Show the tutorial on next startup".

docs.x: Open it with "Try the sample" on the startup screen. It's available in every edition. It's in an A-pose and has 7 texture sets, and each set's base contains an image of the original colors. You may use the sample model only to try PetaNuri3D. Don't use it for any other purpose, and don't extract it or give it to others. If you're new, we recommend painting the sample once all the way through in First steps. To draw without a model, start from "Start a 2D painting" on the startup screen (2D painting).

Open your own 3D model and get ready to paint. You can open FBX, glTF (packed into a single file), GLB, VRM, OBJ and DAE. Click "New" on the startup screen, or choose File → New (Ctrl+N), then pick a 3D model. The texture sets, one for each material, are listed. Choose a Resolution for each set (32 to 4096 px; Lite goes up to 2048). Choose what each set will Start with (the base). You can mix different starting points. Click "Create" and the model appears in the 3D view. To cancel, click "Cancel" or press Esc.

docs.x: Start with What it does Color Starts with the base filled in one color. The default is white. "Model color" uses the material's color instead. Image Uses a PNG, JPEG or similar image as the base. PSD Imports the PSD layers as they are. lilToon material Imports settings, textures and masks from a .mat, or from a .unitypackage that contains one (Load a lilToon material). If the images the model uses are next to the model (in the same folder or a Texture folder) or inside the model, they're found automatically and the set starts with "Image". With "Bulk" at the top, you can set the same resolution for all sets, start all sets with a white base, or choose images and PSDs in one go. A file named the same as a set (body.psd → body) goes into that set. Dropping images, PSDs or .mat files onto this screen sorts them out the same way. Materials that use the same image are combined into one texture set. (Use "Merge ▾" on a row to merge or separate them by hand.) When they're merged, you paint on one texture and it shows on all the materials. Turn on "Open Easy Bake after creation" and choose the target sets, and the Easy Bake window opens once the model loads. You can make an undercoat for skin and clothes before painting in detail (Easy Bake).

Dropping a model on the window doesn't open it: Once a model is open, dropping another one does nothing. Open it with File → New or File → Reload model. A message says a texture wasn't found: Choose the image with "Choose <name>" on the row. Some areas can't be painted: If the model has areas you can't paint, such as faces without UVs, a notice appears at the lower right when you open it. Areas whose UVs are outside the 0 to 1 range are painted at the position where the texture repeats to the same color.

Your work is saved to a project file (.petanuri). The model and all layers and settings go into one file. Making texture images (PNG, PSD) is a separate step: "Export". To do this Do this Save File → Save project file (Ctrl+S) Save under another name File → Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) Open your work to continue File → Open project file (Ctrl+O). You can also drop the file onto the window Open recent work File → Recent files Recover after a crash File → Open from autosave (the newest 3 for each project) Hand it over without the model File → Save without model (FBX) (when it's opened, you choose your own copy of the model) An asterisk (*) in the title means there are unsaved changes. If you close with unsaved changes, you're asked "Save and quit", "Quit without saving" or "Cancel". Autosave runs every 5 minutes. You can also create, open, save, undo and redo from the icons at the right end of the menu bar.

docs.x: Autosave uses a "fast format" that doesn't write the transparent areas of layers. If you have many layers with only lines, saving is much faster. Project files you save by hand use the same format if you turn on "Save project files in the fast format (opens in v1.2.0 or later)" in File → Preferences → Painting → Performance.

The app crashed or froze: Click × again to quit (unsaved changes are lost). Reopen the app and use File → Open from autosave to open the latest autosave. "The app's internal file access has stopped" appears: This can happen after the PC wakes from sleep. Quit, reopen the app and recover your work with File → Open from autosave. A file opened with "(incomplete)" added to its name: Part of that project file couldn't be read. To avoid overwriting the original file, saving becomes "Save as". The save dialog doesn't come back: Check whether the dialog for choosing where to save is hidden behind another window. If it lasts longer than 30 seconds, click × or press Ctrl+S to choose "Wait" or "Stop the previous save and continue". A confirmation appeared when you saved during a preview: While previewing a transform, filter or similar, you're first asked "Apply and continue", "Discard preview and continue" or "Cancel".

When you've fixed a 3D model (FBX etc.), this keeps your painting and updates only the shape. Choose File → Reload model (keep painting). Click "Reload the same file" or "Choose file". Texture sets are matched by material name. Sets with the same name keep their layers and settings as they are.

PetaNuri3D comes in three editions. You can see your current edition in the window title, on the badge on the startup screen, and in Help → "About PetaNuri3D". In this manual, features available in Standard and above are marked with, and Pro-only features with. Features without a badge work from Lite. Compare Lite (free) Standard Pro Drawing, painting, erasing, blending colors, fill, symmetry, UV, selections, transforms, text, rulers, auto fill, PNG export, saving project files, 2D painting, converting luminance to opacity, painting from Unity ✓ ✓ ✓ Layers (per texture set, including the base) Up to 4 Unlimited Unlimited Resolution Up to 2048 Up to 4096 Up to 4096 PSD import and export — ✓ ✓ Filters, adjustment layers, strokes — ✓ ✓ Exporting and importing brush settings (.petabrush) — ✓ ✓ Poses, blend shapes, vertex groups — — ✓ Final look (how lilToon and MToon appear), material settings, paint target, Main color 2nd/3rd, loading and exporting lilToon materials — — ✓ Easy Bake, baking shading and the like, Bake AO, Paint from UV edges — — ✓ AI integration run_js (a command that runs a program inside the app) — — ✓ Features that Lite can't use are dimmed in menus and on buttons, with a small lock icon. Click one to see which edition unlocks it. In Standard, entry points for Pro-only features aren't shown (Help → "Upgrade to Pro" is shown). There's no watermark. There's no limit on the number of texture sets. You can open project files made in any edition. Layers beyond the limit, and settings for features your edition can't use, are kept rather than deleted and remain when you save. For prices and how to buy, see Price on the introduction page. Lite, Standard, Pro and the upgrade to Pro are distributed on BOOTH.

docs.x: You can see the current version next to the title on the startup screen and in Help → "About PetaNuri3D". Changes are listed in the Changelog. When you launch the app (at most once a day), a notice appears at the lower right of the screen if there's a new version. Click "Update now" and the app fetches the new version from the official site, verifies it, replaces the old one after a single confirmation and restarts. If you have unsaved changes, it asks before closing. You can check any time with Help → "Check for updates". File → Preferences → System, "Automatically download and install new versions", is on from the start. When it's on, the app fetches the update at launch and asks "Install and restart" (you can stop it with "Cancel" while it's downloading). If you turn it off, the app fetches the update only when you click "Update now". If you turn off "Check for updates at startup", the app doesn't check when it launches. To update by hand, extract the new ZIP and run setup.exe (it installs over the old one). The same goes for switching editions. Your settings, project files, brushes and upgrade carry over. Only the version number is checked. Your artwork and settings are never sent anywhere. When you're offline, nothing appears.

Left: The toolbar, plus Sub tool, Tool properties, Brush size and Reference image. Right: Three columns. Right next to the 3D view are Texture set, Layer properties and Layer. Next to those are Color, Color values, Color set | Recent colors (as tabs) and History. docs.x: Drag the border between columns, or between rows, to change the width or height. Double-click a border to restore it. Drag the heading to move it, and use the handle at the bottom right to resize it. Click the heading to collapse it. There is no ×. To hide it, use Display → Windows, or right-click the heading → "Hide this panel". Panels stay inside the app window. They cannot go into a separate window outside the app.

Put a ✓ on Display → Windows → "Lock panel layout" to stop panels from being moved or resized. This prevents accidental moves. Even while the layout is locked, you can still move and resize floating windows by dragging the heading. With the lock at the top right of a floating window, you can lock or unlock just that window. When it is locked, it does not move or change size (this is remembered the next time you open it).

docs.x: The toolbar starts on the left. You can attach it above, below or on the right of the work area, or let it float. Drag the toolbar's handle (the top edge when it is vertical, the left edge when it is horizontal). Docking targets appear on the four sides of the work area. Release on a target to attach the toolbar to that edge. At the top or bottom, the tools line up horizontally and wrap if they do not fit. If you release anywhere else, it floats. A floating toolbar switches between "Horizontal" and "Vertical", and double-clicking the handle returns it to its previous edge. You can also choose Left, Right, Top, Bottom or Float from a button's right-click menu → "Toolbar position". The position is remembered the next time you start the app. Right-click a button → "Toolbar icon size" to choose large or small, and "Toolbar columns" to choose "Columns: Auto" or "Columns: Always 1". Tools that do not fit can be scrolled with the wheel, the arrows at the edge, or by dragging with the pen. Reorder: Drag the buttons (a pen works too) into any order. Release after moving a little to reorder, or release without moving to select that tool. Right-click → "Reset order" returns them to the original order. Theme color: The sun and moon switch at the very end of the toolbar toggles between Light and Dark (Dark mode). Hide: Remove the ✓ from Display → Windows → "Toolbar". Toolbox: Display → Windows → "Toolbox" shows a panel with the tool icons in a grid. Like other panels, you can put it in a column or tab, and it wraps to fit the width. Click the foreground color below it to open the Color panel, click the background color or ⇄ to swap them, and click the small black-and-white icon or press D to return to black and white.

docs.x: Line up your favorite tools and sub tools in a small strip above the 3D view and the UV view, so you can switch to them quickly. docs.h: Move the view with the 3D navigator
docs.x: You can tilt the 3D view like a sheet of paper, to an angle that is easy to draw at. Shift+wheel rotates it 5° at a time, and ⟲ and ⟳ on the 3D navigator rotate it 15° at a time. You can also drag the round arrow left and right. If the cursor is over the UV pane, it rotates the UV. While the view is rotated, painting, selecting, panning and right-drag rotation all work as usual. Drags move in the direction you see. In Key bindings, you can also assign keys to "Rotate view left (15°)", "Rotate view right (15°)" and "Reset view rotation" (no keys at first).

docs.h: Move the view with the 3D navigator
docs.x: Drag the handle (…) at the top to move it anywhere. Double-click it to return the navigator to the top right. Drag the left edge, the bottom edge or the bottom-left corner to resize it. You can also change it with "3D navigator size" in File → Preferences → Interface. Click "—" to shrink it into an icon at the bottom right. Click the icon to bring it back (or use Display → Windows → "3D navigator (bring it back with the icon at bottom right)"). You can show rotation and zoom sliders below the navigator. Turn on "Show rotation/zoom sliders on the navigator" in File → Preferences → Interface (off at first). They appear on both the 3D navigator and the UV guide.

docs.h: View another angle at the same time in a small window
docs.x: Shows a small 3D view from a second camera inside the 3D view. While you draw, you can check how it looks from the opposite side or from the side. The small window is for viewing only. You draw in the large view. Click the alternate-angle mini view icon at the bottom right of the 3D view (or use Display → Windows → "Alternate-angle mini view"). Choose the direction (Front, Right, Back, Left, Top, Opposite) from the small window's heading. "Opposite" is the opposite side of the viewpoint of the large view. Drag inside the small window to rotate it, and pan with the middle button or Shift+drag. Zoom in and out with the wheel or Ctrl+drag (drag up to zoom in; handy with a pen), and double-click for Frame all. Move it by its heading, and resize it from the left edge, the top edge and the top-left corner. Close it with ✕.

docs.x: Choose from the same row of icons, or from Display → Shading. The choices are "Single-sided display (back faces are not drawn)" and "Double-sided display (paint visible back faces too)". docs.h: Change how it looks (shading and light direction)
docs.x: Click the ▼ below the shading icon. Drag the sphere to set the direction the light comes from. You can also change it with the handles for horizontal angle and height. Turn on "Follow camera" and the light falls the same way even when you rotate the view. "Reset to default" restores the original. Two-tone toon, Shaded and Final look use the same light. In "Painted colors as-is", you cannot see the light. These are the same values as "Display and lighting" in the Material panel. When the camera control is "Alt + mouse buttons", Shift+right-drag rotates the light horizontally.

docs.h: Change how it looks (shading and light direction)
docs.x: Areas you painted with the Eraser or a transparent color show a checkerboard underneath in 3D. Turn off Display → Shading → "Show transparent areas as a checkerboard" and they turn gray. Right-click a texture set row (or "…") → "Alpha cutout (hide transparency in 3D)" to choose how transparency is shown: "None", "Cutout" (areas fainter than 50% opacity are cut out so you can see through them) and "Transparent" (see-through at the actual opacity). Alpha cutout also changes only how it looks, and the exported images do not change. It is kept in the project file and can be undone. You cannot click cut-out areas in 3D, so paint them in the UV pane.

docs.h: Change how it looks (shading and light direction)
docs.x: Shows the texture in 3D without interpolation, as one square per pixel. It is meant for low-resolution textures such as 32 or 64 px, and for pixel art. Switch it for each texture set, using ⋯ on the set's row or right-click → "Show as pixels (no interpolation)". A set that has it on shows a square badge on its row (click the badge to turn it off). Sets of 256 px or less have it on from the start (automatic). Sets you switched yourself are kept in the project file, and "Reset pixel display to automatic" returns them. Display → Shading → "Show all sets' textures as pixels (no interpolation)" switches all the sets at once. The UV pane always shows pixels when you zoom in.

docs.h: Change how it looks (shading and light direction)

It works only when you draw with a pen (Windows Ink) using a round, hard pen or brush. While it is on, the "Predicted preview line" is not shown. Predicted preview line: Draws the end of the line you are drawing tentatively, as far as the predicted next movement, to hide lag. It is only for hard round pens. Long press on buttons: With "Release to confirm", a long press is confirmed when you release (open the menu with the pen side button). With "Long press opens the right-click menu", a long press opens the menu. In places that are not buttons, such as layer rows, a long press opens the menu either way. Pen side buttons are covered in Pen buttons and Windows Ink.

I turned on "Show pen strokes early" but nothing changes: It works only when you draw with a pen (Windows Ink). Once you open a model, you can draw right away. You don't have to select a texture set first: the app automatically switches to the texture set where you start drawing (for example, body). Click "Pen" on the toolbar at the left (P). Choose "G-pen" in the Sub tool panel. Choose a foreground color in the Color panel. Trace over the model in the 3D view. A line appears where you traced. To rotate, right-drag (the pen's side button) or Space+drag. To zoom in, use the wheel. If you make a mistake, press Ctrl+Z to undo one stroke at a time.

docs.x: Shift+click: Draws a straight line from the end of the previous line. Ctrl+Alt+drag left or right: Changes the brush size. Ctrl+right-drag (pen side button): Dragging left or right changes the brush size, and up or down changes the hardness. Ctrl+dragging with the pen tip changes the opacity left or right and the tip angle up or down. If you draw with the eraser end of the pen, it erases. Alt+right-click on the model to select the texture set at that spot (Select a texture set). You can draw on the UV view with the same tools (UV and visible area). For camera control schemes and other keys, see Pen and mouse controls.

Nothing is painted when you trace: The reason appears in the bar at the bottom of the screen. You can't draw on hidden layers, locked layers or folders. Select a layer you can draw on in the Layers panel (Layers). Color doesn't appear in only some areas: You can't draw outside the selection or on hidden areas. On a layer with Lock transparency on, you can't draw on transparent areas. You can't draw on other texture sets: "Switch to the set where you start drawing" is off. Turn it on from the right-click menu in the 3D view. When there is a selection, you can't draw on sets that are not selected. Pen pressure doesn't change the thickness: Check whether "Pen pressure to size" in Tool properties is on. If it's on and nothing changes, see When pen pressure doesn't work.

Press and release a tool's key to switch to that tool. If you hold the key while drawing, it is that tool only while held, and when you release it you return to the previous tool. The "Hold time" (0.15 to 2 seconds, 0.5 seconds by default) can be changed in File → Preferences → Action → Keyboard. You can turn off this temporary switching in the same place. Hand: while it is selected, dragging with the left button or pen moves the view. In the 3D view, hold Ctrl to zoom. The Eraser's "Through all layers" erases all visible layers at once. Turn on "Don't erase base layers" to keep the base. Display → Windows → "Toolbox" also shows a panel with the tools arranged in a grid. The foreground and background color squares are lined up below it.

docs.x: The values in Tool properties are remembered for each sub tool. To keep the same pen at different thicknesses, duplicate it and give the copy another name. The icons under the sub tool list let you, from the left, "Duplicate", "Name", "Delete", "Reset", "Export", "Export all" and "Import". Right-clicking gives the same options. You can also rename by double-clicking. Drag to reorder (this works with the pen as is). "Small", "Medium" and "Large" above the list change the tile size. Making the tiles smaller gives more room to the Tool properties below. Right-click a toolbar button or a sub tool tile → "Assign key" to give it any key you like. To give the same key to several sub tools, choose "Share (cycle on each press)", and each press moves to the next sub tool. With "Export", "Export all" and "Import", you can exchange brush settings as .petabrush files. Imported tip images are included. You can also import a .petabrush by dropping it onto the window. Deleting a sub tool can't be undone. In Standard and above, you can keep a copy first with "Export".
docs.s: Add, reorder and assign keys to sub tools

docs.x: Click "Import" under the sub tool list. Choose .abr, .gbr, .gih, .sut, images (such as PNG), or a .zip that bundles them. You can choose any number of files. A sub tool that uses the tip is added and selected. You can draw with it right away. You can also import by dropping files onto the Sub tool panel. If you drop an image onto the 3D or UV view, it is treated as an image, not a brush. What is imported is the tip shape and name, the initial size and, when it can be read, the spacing and anti-aliasing. The original app's stroke feel, color mixing and color are not carried over, so adjust them in Tool properties. .abr supports image tips in versions 1, 2 and 6, and .gbr supports versions 1 and 2. .gih uses up to 128 frames at random. .sut makes a tip from the image inside (it may contain things such as a reduced preview image). The limit is 64 MB per file. For a .zip, it is 512 files and 64 MB after extraction. If a format can't be read, the reason is shown. You can import in any edition. Imported tips and sub tools are kept after the next launch.
docs.s: Import brushes from other paint apps

docs.x: The "Brush collection" on the toolbar contains 33 textured brushes. They are a brush set published under CC0 (public domain), converted to this app's settings. You can use them freely, both for your artwork and commercially. Airbrush (large) / Basic spread / Oval brush / Pressure-width brush / Detail brush / Pencil H (sketch) / Mechanical pencil / Pencil 2B / Fine brush (grainy) / Ink brush line art / Fine brush (hard edge, rock texture) / Block brush (layering) / Flat brush (layering) / Charcoal (soft) / Round brush (layering) / Layering (textured) / Shaping (textured) / Thick ink brush (textured) / Ink brush (tilt for volume) / Ink brush (blending in) / Rake brush (grainy) / Impasto (canvas) / Watercolor edge / Scattered texture / Canvas rub / Dry scratch / Splatter (large) / Splatter (light) / Squiggle / Textured base / Large sponge / Grainy noise / Leaves The blurs and smudges from the same collection (Rake blur (smudge), Textured blur, Flat blur) are under "Blend", and the erasers (Eraser (chalk tip), Kneaded eraser (soft)) are under "Eraser". The "Bundled brushes" tips (31) and the "Built-in" paper textures (6) can also be used with other sub tools. The feel is not exactly the same as the original brushes.

The Pen's "Pixel pen" paints crisply as many pixels as the brush size, snapped to the pixel grid of the texture. A size of 1 paints 1 pixel and 3 paints 3×3, and colors do not mix. It suits pixel art and low-resolution textures such as 32 or 64 px. The size is in texture px. Pen pressure and taper do not change the thickness. In the 3D view, it paints only inside the island of the face visible at the center of the pen tip. Symmetry also works (it paints the same pixel on the other side too). Other pens paint the same way if you turn on "Pixel (crisp, snapped to the texel grid)" in Tool properties. If you show the texture as pixels, the pixels also look square in 3D (⋯ on the texture set row → "Show as pixels (no interpolation)"; see Texture sets).

In the Tool properties panel, you set how the selected sub tool feels. The "~" line at the very top is a sample drawn with the current settings. When you change a setting, it updates immediately. This prevents thin lines from appearing at seams. The width is the same value as the export bleed (Bleed) Tip The shape of the pen tip, such as round, square or pencil (Choose the tip) Hardness How crisp the edge is. Lowering it blurs the edge Spacing The gap between tips. Widening it gives a row of dots Stabilization How strongly line wobble is suppressed (Stabilization type) Pen pressure to size, Minimum size Whether pen pressure changes the thickness, and the thickness at the lightest pressure Pen pressure to opacity Whether pen pressure changes how dark the stroke is Anti-aliasing Smooths the edges Build-up (darker with each pass), Flow The more you go over the same spot, the darker it gets (suited to airbrushes). docs.x: In the "Brush size" panel on the left, click a frequently used size to select it. Clicking changes only the size (set opacity and hardness in Tool properties). The pencil at the end of the size tiles, or a right-click, gives "Add current size", "Remove selected" and "Reset". "Remove this size" in the right-click menu removes the tile you clicked right away. The panel wraps by width, so if you make it narrow it shrinks down to one column. [ ] also change the thickness. In the key bindings you can also assign keys to "Next larger size in the brush size list" and "Next smaller size in the brush size list". When a shape tool is selected, this changes the shape's line width (up to 500). With Polygon fill and Select by face, it changes the "Pick radius" (up to 200). The "Size basis" decides how thickness behaves when you zoom in or out. You choose it for each sub tool. Size basis Thickness Follow settings (default) Follows the "Brush size unit" in File → Preferences → Painting. The default is "screen px" Fixed on texture Paints the same thickness on the texture whether you zoom in or out (on screen it looks thicker when you zoom in) Variable on screen The thickness stays the same on the screen. When you zoom in it paints thinner on the texture, and when you zoom out it paints thicker
docs.s: Set the thickness (brush size, size basis)

docs.x: Choose it with "3D brush projection" for Pen, Brush, Brush collection, Eraser and Blur. "Follow the surface" (the default) makes lines less likely to stretch on slanted faces and edges, and image tips also line up with the direction of the face. "Match the screen" projects from the camera, so lines stretch on slanted faces. When you draw in the UV view, both work the same way.
docs.s: Keep lines from stretching on slanted faces (3D brush projection)

docs.x: Click "Tip" to choose. There are round, square, flat brush, pencil, chalk, spray, watercolor, ink brush, sparkle, star and heart tips, plus 31 bundled brush tips. With "Load" in the tip list, you can also make a tip from an image (a PNG or JPEG with a black shape on a white background), from brushes of other paint apps (.abr, .gbr, .gih, .sut), or from a .zip that bundles them. For image tips, "Angle", "Random rotation" and "Rotate along stroke" appear.

If you choose a "Paper texture" for Pen, Brush, Eraser and so on, paper or canvas grain is added to the darkness of the paint. It repeats over the texture, so it sticks to the surface and doesn't slide when you move the view. You can choose from the 6 built-in textures and the 15 patterns (the same designs as Pattern). With "Import texture" you can also use any image (lighter areas take more paint). Adjust it with "Texture scale", "Texture angle", "Texture strength" and "Invert texture brightness". Where a UV island is upside down or sideways, use "Texture angle" to match the direction of the pattern. "Apply mode" is either "Multiply (brighter areas take more paint)" or "Subtract (dark areas drop out first)".

Stabilization type How it works Smooth (follows with delay) Follows the pen tip with a slight delay and smooths the line 1€ (strength varies with speed) When you draw slowly it strongly suppresses wobble, and when you draw fast it reduces lag. Adjust it with "Stabilization when slow" and "Relax when fast" String (follows at a fixed distance) It follows at a distance of "String length" from the pen tip. Hand tremor disappears Start/end taper: The length over which the start and end of a stroke are thinned. The end taper redraws the end of the line thinner when you lift the pen, so there is no lag while you draw. Motion: "Speed to size", "Size jitter", "Opacity jitter", "Tilt to size", "Tilt to opacity", "Rotate tip by pen tilt direction" and "Rotate tip by pen twist". Tilt and twist work only with pens that send them. Pressure curve (size/opacity): Move the points to decide how pen pressure responds (horizontal is pressure, vertical is size or opacity). Double-click to return to a straight line. Stroke feel: In File → Preferences → Pen & input → "Stroke feel", "How tapering is made" lets you choose "Taper by pressure only (default)" or "Taper by length". Taper by pressure only makes a blob at the start or a thread-like tail at the end less likely (for pens only. A mouse always tapers by length).

Lines get thinner when you zoom in and thicker when you zoom out: Set "Size basis" to "Fixed on texture". Lines stretch on slanted faces: Set "3D brush projection" to "Follow the surface". Lines appear after a delay behind the pen tip: Lower "Stabilization", or set "Stabilization type" to "1€ (strength varies with speed)". Also try "Show pen strokes early (reduce lag)" under "Reduce lag" in File → Preferences → Pen & input. A blob forms at the start of a stroke, or a tail appears at the end: Set the stroke feel to "Taper by pressure only (default)". Thin lines remain at UV seams: Turn on "Paint into padding outside islands in 3D too".

docs.h: Also paint back and hidden faces
docs.x: This paints areas that are hard to see because they wrap around, such as the inside of hair, overlapping clothing and the gaps between fingers, all at once. Turn it on and off with "Also paint back and hidden faces" just below Opacity in Tool properties (for the Eraser, "Also erase back and hidden faces"). Centered on the face visible under the pen tip, it also paints the back and inside faces that the camera can't see, within a sphere that looks the same size as the brush circle. Pen, Brush, Brush collection, Eraser and Gradient are on from the start. Decoration, Pattern and Stitch are off at first. When it is off, only the visible faces are painted. It isn't available for Blur, Smudge, Blend and Stamp (because they use the colors or image shown on the screen). It doesn't matter in the UV view (it already applies to all faces). Hardness blurs the edge. Image tips attach to the inner faces in the same shape you see on the screen. Selection, hidden areas, symmetry and Lock transparency work as usual. If you paint a thick part, the paint reaches the other side. Make the brush smaller, or turn it off to paint only the visible faces.

docs.h: Choose colors and use the eyedropper
docs.x: The color you draw with (the foreground color) is chosen with the Color panel, the Color values panel, Recent colors or Color sets. Whichever you use, it becomes the same foreground color. Color: Buttons at the top switch the picker type. There are 5: "Ring + square", "Ring + triangle", "Square + hue bar", "Disc + value bar" and "Sliders (RGB/HSV)". Color values: The foreground and background colors, HEX, picking a color from the screen, RGB/HSV numbers and opacity. The ▾ on the right expands the numbers and ▴ collapses them. Recent colors: The last 12 colors you actually painted with or picked (newest first). Click one to make it the foreground color. When the RGB/HSV sliders appear below the color picker, switch between them with the "RGB" and "HSV" buttons. The format you choose is kept after the next launch.

docs.h: Choose colors and use the eyedropper
docs.x: X (or ⇄) swaps the foreground and background colors. D (or the small button at the bottom left of the two squares) resets the foreground color to black and the background color to white. Alt+Backspace fills with the foreground color, and Ctrl+Backspace fills with the background color. If there is a selection, it fills inside it. If not, it fills the whole of the selected layer.

docs.h: Choose colors and use the eyedropper
docs.x: The eyedropper (I) picks the color where you click. The sub tools are "Sample displayed color" (the color you see) and "Sample from layer" (the color of the selected layer). While you hold Alt, any tool acts as the eyedropper. If the camera controls are set to Alt + mouse buttons, use I in the 3D view. You can also pick a color with right-click in the 3D view → "Pick color here". Raising "Sample area" takes the average of the surrounding colors. While the eyedropper is in use, a round magnifier appears at the cursor. The frame in the middle is where the color is taken from, and the outer ring is the color you get. You can turn it off with "Show magnifier" in Tool properties.

docs.h: Choose colors and use the eyedropper
docs.x: Click the eyedropper icon in the Color values panel (Shift+I). A magnifier and a loupe showing the color values appear. Click the spot you want. You can pick from outside the window too. Enter and Space also pick. The arrow keys move 1 pixel at a time (10 pixels with Shift). Esc or right-click cancels. It picks from a snapshot of the screen taken when you started, so videos and the like look frozen.

docs.x: Click a swatch to make it the foreground color. "+ Current color" adds one, drag to reorder, and double-click to name a swatch. "Replace" and "Delete" act on the selected swatch. You can undo deleting a swatch with Ctrl+Z. "Small", "Medium" and "Large" change the swatch size. The "…" menu lets you create, duplicate, rename and delete sets, export (JSON / .gpl palette) and import. A .gpl can be imported by dropping it anywhere on the window. Drag while holding Space to scroll the list (for pens).

docs.h: Choose colors and use the eyedropper
docs.x: In the Reference image panel, bring up an image by clicking "Open", dropping a file onto the panel, or clicking the panel and pressing Ctrl+V. Click or drag on the image to pick that color. When you release, it goes into Recent colors. The magnifier icon at the top zooms in and out, "100%" sets actual size, and the corner icon fits the whole image. It can also be operated with the pen alone. The image you bring up comes back the next time you launch.

docs.h: Draw with transparency (erase with the same brush)
docs.x: Use the checkerboard button in the Color values panel, or C, to make the foreground color transparent. You can then erase color from the current layer while keeping the tip, hardness and pen pressure of Pen, Brush, Brush collection and so on. To switch back, press C or the checkerboard button again. Clicking the foreground color square or choosing a color also switches back. With the transparent color, Fill (Fill island, Whole material, Fill enclosed area), Polygon fill and Shape also erase the area they would paint. Gradient erases more strongly toward the foreground-color side. Stamp does not erase, even with the transparent color. You can't erase on a layer with Lock transparency on. To erase, turn off Lock transparency first.

docs.x: When you draw on one side, the same thing appears on the other. Use it when you draw the same shape on both sides, such as the left and right of a face or clothing. Click "X" (left/right) at the top left of the 3D view (M). Draw on one side of the model. The same thing appears on the other side. "Y" (front/back) and "Z" (up/down) can also be used in any combination at the same time (X and Z together paint in 4 places). You can also toggle it from the Edit menu, or with right-click in the 3D view → "Paint symmetrically". "Symmetry X/Y/Z" also appears at the very top of Tool properties and in the heading of the UV view (it is the same switch as the one at the top left of the 3D view). One Undo reverses both sides together.

docs.x: The ▼ next to X, Y and Z lets you choose the mirror center from "Model center", "Origin" and "Custom". Use it when the center is off from the middle of the body, for example with an outfit-only FBX. Model center: For left/right, this is the place where the shape is most symmetric. Even if there are decorations or accessories on one side only, it stays at the middle of the body. Origin: Mirrors at the origin of the coordinates. Custom: Enter the center as X, Y and Z in cm, or use "Click on the model to set" to use the point you click. If "Snap to vertex" is on (the default), the position of the vertex nearest to the point you clicked is used. You can also set it with right-click in the 3D view → "Paint symmetrically" → "Set symmetry center here". When you set it, the mirror plane appears semi-transparent in 3D for about 2 seconds. The custom position is saved in the project file.

Item Default Details Mirror partner search range 1% 0 to 3%. When there is no surface at the mirrored point (for example clothes that differ slightly on the left and right), the nearest surface within this range is painted as the other side. 0% paints only at the exact mirrored point Mirror painting on hidden parts (3D brushes) Off With one side hidden by the visible area or Hide pen, it also paints the other side from the visible side. It works with the 3D Pen, Brush, Eraser and Stamp (not with the UV view, Fill, Blur, Smudge or Blend) Show symmetry guides, Symmetry guide strength On Shows the line of the symmetry center in 3D. The strength is 10 to 100% Show cursor on the mirrored side On Also shows a dotted circle at the mirrored position of where you paint. If the other side is behind or inside a surface, it appears faint All of these settings are kept after the next launch.

○ means it works, △ means conditions apply, × means it doesn't work and ― means not relevant. If you choose a tool that symmetry doesn't work with, the symmetry field at the top of Tool properties is dimmed and shows the reason. Tool 3D view UV view Pen, Brush, Brush collection, Decoration, Pattern, Stitch ○ ○ Eraser (including Through all layers) ○ ○ Stamp ○ ○ (the image is also flipped on the mirrored side) Blur, Smudge ○ ○ Blend ○ ― (a tool you can't use in the UV view) Liquify ○ ○ Fill (island, whole material), Fill enclosed area ○ ○ Polygon fill ○ ○ Shape ○ ○ Gradient △ △ Text, Paste image ○ ○ (also applied to the mirrored side when you confirm) Selection pen, Selection eraser, Select by face ○ ○ Selection (Rectangle, Ellipse, Lasso, Polyline, Auto select, Select by island) × × (tools that define an area by enclosing it) Move/transform ― × (an operation that moves existing artwork) Eyedropper, placing a ruler ― ― (lines drawn along a ruler are symmetric) Hide pen × × (a tool that hides parts of the display) △ Gradient: In the 3D view, visible faces keep their direct color, and what goes onto the mirrored side is the faces that are not visible. In the UV view, with a gradient that includes transparency, the darker side goes in. When "Also paint back and hidden faces" is on, every face is painted directly by the 3D line, so symmetry is not used. Even when the model is posed, it paints the symmetric spot in the original pose (the rest pose). Even if one arm is bent, it goes to the same place on the other arm (Poses).

It appears at a shifted spot on the other side: The mirror center is off. Set the center to "Origin" or "Custom" with ▼ (Set the mirror center). It doesn't appear on part of the other side: The shape differs slightly between left and right there. Raise "Mirror partner search range" in ▼. It doesn't appear on the other side after you hide one side: Turn on "Mirror painting on hidden parts (3D brushes)" in ▼. Drawing in the UV view doesn't appear on the other side: If the other side is in a different texture set (material), it doesn't appear in the UV view. Draw in the 3D view. X, Y and Z have a slash through them: Symmetry doesn't work with the current tool (Which tools it works with).

The Blend tool (J) blends the colors you painted. All of its sub tools calculate on the 3D surface, so they don't break at UV seams. Sub tool What it does Main settings Blur, Blur (strong, wide), Blur (weak, edges only) Smooths where you trace. The more you trace and the more you go back and forth, the more the colors melt together "Blur spread", "Blend more with each pass", "3D brush projection" Smudge, Smudge (strong stretch), Smudge (soft) Drags the color and stretches it "Strength" Blend, Blend (smooth), Blend (thick) Picks up the color where you trace and carries it, painting while mixing with the foreground color "Paint amount", "Color stretch", "Sample color from all layers" Rake blur (smudge), Textured blur, Flat blur These are the blur and smudge sub tools from the bundled Brush collection — How strongly it acts is set with "Strength" (it corresponds to opacity for other brushes). "Paint amount" is the proportion of foreground color. At 0, it only blends the colors that are already painted. Raising "Color stretch" carries the picked-up color further. "Blend more with each pass" (on by default): The more times you trace the same spot, the more it melts together. There is a limit so that continuing to rub in one stroke doesn't melt even the line art. When it is off, going over the same spot within one stroke does not make it stronger. When "3D brush projection" for Blur is "Follow the surface", the area that gets blurred has the same shape as the pen. You can also choose a tip in Tool properties for Blur, Smudge and Blend. Blur and Smudge can also be used in the UV view. Blend is available only in the 3D view.

docs.x: This distorts the existing drawing where you trace. Use it when you want to adjust the shape of a line a little. Sub tool What it does Push Drags the drawing in the direction you move Bloat, Pinch Spreads the traced area outward, or pulls it inward Twirl (right), Twirl (left) Twists clockwise or counterclockwise Undo Gradually returns the traced area to the drawing as it was before liquify began "Strength" (it also changes with pen pressure), "Hardness" (how the edge acts) and the brush size are the same as for other brushes. Bloat, Pinch, Twirl and Undo act in proportion to the length you trace. Each stroke can be undone with one press of Ctrl+Z. The drawing doesn't get blurry however many times you trace. In the 3D view, it connects across UV breaks. The closer you zoom in, the finer it acts. In the UV view, it distorts only inside UV islands. It respects Selection and Lock transparency. Symmetry also works.

docs.x: Fill (G) fills a UV island, an area enclosed by lines and so on in one go. If you create the layer to fill below the line layer, the lines stay clean. Sub tool What it fills Fill island The whole UV island you click Whole material The whole material you click Fill enclosed area An area enclosed by lines: the connected area of similar color within that island (Details) Lasso fill The area you enclose by dragging (Details) Polygon fill The whole face you trace (Details) With Fill island and Whole material, you can change "Anti-aliasing (island edges)" and the opacity.

docs.x: Create a layer to fill below the line art layer and select it. Choose the Fill sub tool "Fill enclosed area". Set "Reference" in Tool properties to "All layers" (when you drew the lines on another layer). Click the area you want to fill. It stops at the lines and is filled with the foreground color. Setting Details Reference Looks for the lines to stop at in the artwork of "All layers" or "Selected layer" Tolerance How much color difference is treated as the same Close gaps 0 to 5. Thickens the lines so that small breaks stop the fill (n closes breaks up to about 2n px) Expand/contract -3 to 3. + makes the fill go under the lines and removes the white gap between the fill and the lines Anti-aliasing (smooth edges by 1px) Smooths the edge of the fill

docs.x: Drag to enclose an area in the 3D view, UV view or 2D canvas, and the enclosed area is filled with the foreground color. The current selection is kept as it is, and one Undo reverts the fill. If you enclose an area on a different texture set in the 3D view, it switches to the set that appears most in the enclosed area and then fills.
docs.s: Fill an area with the lasso

docs.x: This fills the whole face you trace with the foreground color. The pick radius is the size of the circle at the pen tip. If you turn off "Fill per quad (2 triangles as 1 face)", it fills triangle by triangle. If you turn on "Mesh wireframe" at the top left of the 3D view, you can see the face boundaries (Mesh wireframe).

The fill goes beyond the lines: There is a break in the line. Raise "Close gaps". A white gap remains next to the line: Set "Expand/contract" to +. It doesn't stop at the lines on another layer: Set "Reference" to "All layers". The lines get thinner or chipped: If you fill on the same layer as the lines, the fill covers the lines by the "Expand/contract" amount. Press Ctrl+Z, create a layer to fill below the lines, and fill again.

This paints so that colors change gradually. In the 3D view, drag from the start point to the end point. Click "Gradient" on the toolbar. Choose a sub tool ("Color and opacity", "Foreground → background", "Foreground → transparent" or "Radial (foreground color to transparent)"). In Tool properties, choose "Linear" or "Radial" for "Shape". In the 3D view, drag from the start point to the end point. Release to paint. Linear goes in the direction from the start point to the end point. For Radial, the start point is the center and the length of the drag is the radius. Hold Shift for 45° steps. When "Also paint back and hidden faces" is on (the default), the gradient also applies to the back and inside faces along the 3D line connecting the point you pressed and the point you released (for example, from the roots of hair to its tips). When it is off, only visible faces are painted. It paints the selected layer of the selected texture set. Areas outside the selection and hidden areas are unchanged. You can also draw by dragging in the UV view.
docs.k: gradation fade gradient map ramp color stops linear radial presets transparent hair tips

docs.x: If you set "Color" in Tool properties to "Color and opacity stops", you can paint with a gradient made of several colors and opacities. Click an empty spot on the bar to add a color stop (2 to 32). Select a stop and change its position and opacity. You can also change the position by dragging the stop. Click the selected stop again, or double-click it, and choose a color. Remove a stop with "Remove stop", Delete, or by dragging it down away from the bar. "Use foreground color", "Distribute evenly" and "Swap left/right" are also available. With "Presets ▾", you can choose from 240 presets (some include transparency). You can search by group and name. With "Save current", you can keep your own preset (My presets). Where the opacity is 0, the color below remains. To erase painted color, use the transparent color. To bake shading that follows height or surface orientation into a new layer, the Pro gradient bake is handy.
docs.s: Build it with color and opacity stops

docs.x: Place a center on a face of the model or in the space outside it, and spread color by 3D distance from there. The color does not change when you move the view. Select the layer to paint. Click "Paint from a 3D point" in the Gradient Tool properties. The "3D spatial gradient" window opens. In the 3D view, click a face of the model or an empty spot to place the center. Set how the color spreads with "Spread distance" and the color and opacity stops or presets. It appears on the selected layer right away. Click "Paint on layer" to confirm. After you confirm, one Undo reverts it. If you cancel, the layer goes back to the original drawing. This is an operation for 3D models. On the 2D canvas, draw with an ordinary drag.
docs.s: Spread from a point in 3D space

docs.x: Move the center by dragging the arrows, the plane or the handle at the center, or by entering X, Y and Z coordinates. Use "Pick center in 3D view" to place it again, and "Clear center" to remove it. While you are placing a point, press Esc to cancel. When you place it in space, it goes at the same depth as the current center (or the model's center if there is none yet). "Spread distance" is a percentage (%) of the model's height. Selection, hidden areas, Lock transparency and masks are respected.
docs.s: Move the center and set the spread distance

docs.x: With the Shape tool, you draw lines, rectangles, ellipses, polygons and curves in the foreground color. You can draw in both the 3D view and the UV view. Click "Shape" on the toolbar and choose a form with the sub tool. In the 3D view, drag from the start point to the end point. When you release, it is drawn in the foreground color. Sub tool How to draw Linear Connects the two points you drag. Shift gives 45° steps Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon Fills the inside. Shift gives a square, a circle or an undistorted regular polygon Rectangle (outline), Ellipse (outline), Polygon (outline) Draws only the outline Curve After you drag and release, moving the mouse bends the line. Press again or press Enter to confirm Curve (connect points) Each click places a point (up to 24) and makes a smooth line through the points. Double-click or press Enter to confirm, and press Backspace to remove the last point With "Draw from center" on, the start point becomes the center. The number of "Corners" of a polygon is 3 to 12. A corner points up, and with an even number of corners the top and bottom are flat. With Curve (connect points), turning on "Close (make a loop)" makes a loop, and setting "Painting style" to "Fill" fills the inside. You can use it to fill a free-form shape. "Line width" is linked to the brush size (up to 500). Changing it from the brush size list, [ ] or the popup palette has the same effect. It is kept for each Shape sub tool and does not change the pen's size. If you choose an image tip in Tool properties, it is placed along the outline of the shape (stitches, lace and so on). Choose "Round" to go back to an ordinary line. It applies only to visible faces and counts as one Undo step. While drawing, press Esc to cancel.

docs.h: Change color and size with the pen only (popup palette)
docs.x: If you press and release the pen's side button without moving the pen, a round palette appears on the spot. You can choose frequently used sub tools, the foreground color and the brush size while holding the pen. How to bring it up, how to use each part and the setting for bringing it up with a mouse are covered in Popup palette.

docs.h: You can paint clothes and accessories too
docs.x: You can paint outfits and accessories with the same tools, not only the avatar's body. Below are examples of outfits and accessories from the ののつよ series, opened in PetaNuri3D. To draw a line only inside one part (a UV island), first select that part with "Select by island" in Selection, then draw. Nothing is drawn outside the selection (Selection).

docs.x: Scatters small decorations in the foreground color wherever you drag. Size and direction vary slightly from one to the next. Click "Decoration" on the toolbar. Choose a decoration from the sub tools. Choose a foreground color and drag over the 3D view. The decorations are Sparkle, Star, Heart, Flower, Cherry blossom, Music note, Snowflake, Polka dots, Bubble, Crescent moon, Diamond, Four-leaf clover and Drop, plus four kinds of Lace. Hover over the 3D or UV view to see the shape of the tip. Change Size, Scatter, Random rotation and other settings in Tool properties, as with the Pen (Set how it feels). "Also paint back and hidden faces" is off by default. Symmetry also works.

docs.x: "Lace (scallop)", "Lace (picot)", "Lace (small flowers)" and "Lace (mesh)" line up a pattern like a band along your stroke. The pattern stays connected around curves and sharp corners, and also on the 3D model. The holes are transparent, and the lace is painted in the foreground color. The thickness sets the size of the pattern. If you choose one as the tip of the Shape tool, you can draw lace along the outline of a rectangle or an ellipse (Shape).

Places an imported image on the 3D model. Use it for logos, patches, pattern materials and so on. Click "Stamp" on the toolbar. In Tool properties, click "Import image" to add PNG, JPEG or other images (as many as you like). Choose an image from the list. Click in the 3D view to place one copy of the image. Drag to keep placing copies at the set spacing. Hover over the 3D or UV view to see the image you are about to place as a translucent preview, with its current size, angle, color and opacity. The preview is only a guide before you paint. It is not added to the texture. A faint preview of the next placement also appears ahead, in the direction you are moving. Turn off "Show the next placement faintly" to see only the current preview. The image is placed in its own colors (transparent areas are not placed). Turn on "Paint with foreground color" to use only the image's shape and paint it in the foreground color. The "Stamp (scatter)" sub tool scatters images with varied directions and positions. It applies only to visible faces, and one stroke counts as one Undo step. You can also place stamps in the UV view. Symmetry works in both the 3D and UV views. On the opposite side, the image is mirrored too.
docs.k: decal sticker logo emblem badge patch seal imprint insert clone

docs.x: At the top of Tool properties, you will find a large preview of the current image, the image list, the size and the angle. Setting What it does Size Length of the image's longer side Opacity How strongly the image is placed Spacing Distance between copies when you drag to place them continuously Angle, Random rotation The direction of the image, and how much it varies Size variation, Scatter Variation in size and position Rotate along stroke Rotates the image to follow the direction you drag Size by pen pressure Changes the size with pen pressure Paint with foreground color (use only the image's shape) Paints the shape of the image in the foreground color Show the next placement faintly Shows a preview of where the next copy will go (on by default) Imported images are kept the next time you start the app (up to 60). Use "Remove this image" to take one off the list. You can also turn your own drawings into stamps (2D canvas).

Nothing is placed when I click: No image is selected. Add one with "Import image" and choose it from the list. Click on a visible face of the model. The white box around the image is placed too: The image has no transparent area. Use a PNG with a transparent background. The result differs slightly from the preview: Random rotation, Scatter and the variation settings are not shown in the preview.

A pen that paints only the pattern areas in the foreground color. The pattern repeats on the texture, so it does not shift when you move the view. Click "Pattern" on the toolbar. Choose a pattern from the sub tools or from the swatch list at the top of Tool properties. Choose a foreground color and drag over the clothing. There are 15 patterns: Vertical stripes, Horizontal stripes, Diagonal stripes, Polka dots, Small polka dots, Checkerboard, Gingham, Tartan, Argyle, Herringbone, Denim (twill), Knit, Heart, Star and Crosshatch. Hover over the 3D or UV view to see the pattern to be painted, shown in the foreground color and translucent inside the brush circle. With "Load pattern image", you can use any image as a pattern (brighter areas take more paint). The same patterns are also available from "Paper texture" on other pens and brushes (Paper texture).

docs.x: Setting What it does Pattern size Size of one repeat of the pattern (%). While you adjust it, a preview appears as a larger circle where you last hovered Pattern angle Angle at which the pattern is rotated (°) Pattern strength How strong the pattern is Invert light and dark Swaps the painted and unpainted areas Apply mode "Multiply (brighter areas take more paint)" or "Subtract (dark areas drop out first)"

The pattern is upside down or sideways: The UV island is upside down or sideways. Match the direction with "Pattern angle" before you paint. The pattern is distorted: Where the UVs are distorted, the pattern is distorted too.

Draws decorations that repeat along a line, such as stitches. The stitches rotate to follow the direction of the line. Click "Stitch" on the toolbar. Choose a type of stitch from the sub tools. Choose a foreground color and drag where you want stitches. Sub tool What it draws Stitches (dotted), Stitch (puffy), Seam, Piping, Cross stitch, Zigzag stitch, Studs (rivets) Draw stitches on the current layer in the foreground color. They also work in the 2D canvas Wrinkles (soft groove), Bulge (soft raise) Draw relief by height in the normal map folder The size basis is fixed to "Variable on screen". If you choose Stitch as the tip of the Shape tool, you can line up stitches along the outline of a rectangle or a curve (Shape).

docs.x: Turn on "Draw in the normal map folder" in Tool properties. Set the height with "Height (0 carve, 50 flat, 100 raise)" (shown only when the option is on). Drag over the model. The stroke goes into the "Normal map" folder in the Layers panel (the folder is created if it does not exist) and is drawn by height. When you are done, click "◀ Back to previous layer" at the top center of the 3D view. You return to the layer, display and tool you had before. Wrinkles and Bulge always draw by height in the normal map folder. The relief shows in the final look. If it is hard to see, raise "Normal map strength" in the Material panel. When you export, it becomes a normal map image (Paint target).

docs.h: Turn your drawing into a stamp (2D canvas)
docs.x: On a square canvas for stamps, you draw with the usual tools and layers and can register the result as a stamp as is. Click "Stamp" on the toolbar. Click "Draw in 2D canvas" in Tool properties. The 3D view is hidden, and a square canvas appears in the UV view. Draw with the Pen, Eraser, Fill, Gradient and so on. Click "Register as stamp" at the bottom and enter a name. The combined look of the visible layers becomes the stamp as is. Go back to editing the model and paint with that stamp. Layers, folders, masks, selections and Undo work as usual. The limits for each edition are the same too (Lite allows up to 4 layers). Choose the canvas resolution in the field at the bottom (32 to 4096; Lite goes up to 2048). To go back without registering, click "Return to model editing". What you drew is kept. To edit a registered stamp, click "Redraw this image" in the Stamp tool properties, or right-click an image in the list → Redraw in 2D canvas. When you register again, choose "Overwrite" or "Register under another name". You can also open it with a right-click in the list → Draw new in 2D canvas. The canvas layers are saved with the project file (.petanuri) and with Autosave. The Texture sets panel shows that you are editing a 2D canvas. This canvas is not included in the model's list of texture sets, nor in PNG or PSD exports.

docs.h: Draw in 2D without a model (2D painting)
docs.x: A mode for drawing on a square canvas without opening a 3D model. You start from a transparent base and draw with the usual tools and layers. Click "Start a 2D painting" on the start screen (it is below "Try the sample"). In the "Create a new 2D painting" window, choose the canvas size (32 × 32 to 4096 × 4096). Draw with the Pen, Brush, Gradient and so on. Click "Export PNG" at the bottom to save the combined visible layers as a PNG with transparency. If you save to a project file (.petanuri), you can keep painting later as a 2D painting, with the layers intact. "Register as stamp" also works. You can keep painting in 2D painting after you register. File → Export → Export PSD (selected set) saves a PSD with the layers and folders intact. Lite is limited to a resolution of 2048 and 4 layers, including the base. Standard and Pro go up to 4096, with no limit on the number of layers. The 3D view and features that use the model's shape (baking, poses, materials and so on) are not available.

docs.x: Once you make a selection, drawing, painting, erasing, filters and gradients affect only the inside of it. Use it when you want to paint without going over the edge. Select the "Selection" tool (S). In the sub tools, choose a selection method (Rectangle / Ellipse, Lasso, and so on). In the 3D view or UV view, drag, trace or click to select. The outside dims slightly and a selection outline appears along the boundary. Switch to a pen or another tool and paint. Nothing is applied outside the selection. Press Ctrl+D to deselect.

docs.x: Sub tool How to select Rectangle / Ellipse Drag. Lasso Trace around the area. Polyline Click to place points. Close the shape by clicking the first point, double-clicking, or pressing Enter. Auto select Selects the connected area of colors close to the point you click. Select by island Selects the whole UV island you click. Select by face Selects the whole faces you trace over. Selection pen / Selection eraser Trace with a brush to add or subtract (reversed while you hold Alt). In the 3D view, only visible faces are selected. Turn on "Also select back and hidden faces" in tool properties to select everything that overlaps the shape on screen, including the back. This is handy when you select all the way around the body to paint clothing stripes. For Auto select, set "Reference" (All layers / Selected layer), "Tolerance" and "Anti-aliasing (smooth edges by 1px)" in tool properties. For Select by face, set "Pick radius" and "Select by quads (treat 2 triangles as 1 face)".

In tool properties, choose New, Add, Subtract or Intersect under "Selection mode". If you hold a key before you start dragging, the mode changes for that one stroke only. Key held at the start Selection mode None New (replaces the current selection). Click without moving to deselect Shift Add (adds to the current selection) Alt Subtract (removes from the current selection) Shift+Alt Intersect (keeps only the overlap)
docs.s: Add to or subtract from a selection

docs.x: Ctrl+click a layer thumbnail to select the painted area of that layer (Shift to add, Alt to subtract). Right-click in the 3D view → "Select this island (selection)" to select the island you clicked. The right-click menu in the UV view also has "Add this island to selection". To select all areas close to the foreground color at once, use Select all similar colors.

You can't paint where you want: A leftover selection blocks painting outside it. Press Ctrl+D to deselect. You can't draw on other texture sets: While a selection exists, you can't draw on a texture set that has no selection. Either deselect, or use "Select all" (Ctrl+A), which covers every set. The back isn't selected: In the 3D view, only visible faces are selected. Turn on "Also select back and hidden faces". The outside is too dark to judge colors: Turn off Selection → "Darken outside the selection" and only the selection outline remains (menu).

While a selection exists, the selection bar appears under the 3D view (under the UV view if only the UV is shown). Icon buttons follow the "Selection active" label on the left. Hold the pen tip or cursor over a button to see its name and key. Button What it does Deselect (the colored button) Removes the selection. Even after that, "Reselect" (Ctrl+Shift+D) brings it back Invert Inverts the selection Expand, Contract, Feather Adjust the shape of the selection. On a narrow screen they are grouped under "Modify ▾" Fill Fills the selection with the foreground color Clear Clears the inside of the selection To new layer ▾ "Copy to new layer" and "Cut to new layer" More ▾ Create mask from selection, Show selected only, Hide selected, Show selection outline, Darken outside the selection When the Hide pen bar or a ruler strip is showing, the selection bar sits above it. "Show selected only" and "Hide selected" are Visible area features.

docs.x: The "Selection" menu lists the items for refining and using selections. Most of them are also in the "Selection" submenu of the right-click menu in the 3D view. Item Key What it does Select all Ctrl+A Selects the entire area of every texture set Deselect Ctrl+D Removes the selection Restore selection (last deselected) Ctrl+Shift+D Brings back the last selection you deselected Invert selection Ctrl+Shift+I Selects what isn't selected Expand selection / Contract selection — Grows or shrinks the selection by 1 to 64 px on the UV Feather edge — Softens the edge by 1 to 64 px Select painted area of layer — Selects where the selected layer has paint Select all similar colors (foreground color) — Selects areas close to the foreground color (below) Create mask from selection — Adds a mask in the shape of the selection to the selected layer (Mask) Copy selection to new layer — Copies the artwork inside to a new layer at the same position Cut selection to new layer — Moves the artwork inside to a new layer Fill selection with foreground color — Fills the inside with the foreground color Clear inside selection Delete Erases the artwork inside the selection on the selected layer Show selection outline Ctrl+H Shows or hides the outline (the selection stays, and so does the darkening outside) Darken outside the selection — Turn it off to leave only the outline, so you can paint while seeing the outside colors as they are. The setting is kept the next time you start the app (on by default)

docs.x: Selects areas close to the foreground color across the whole texture, including areas that aren't connected. Use it, for example, when you change the shadow color for each base color. With the Eyedropper (I), set the color you want to select as the foreground color. Choose Selection → "Select all similar colors (foreground color)". Use "Fuzziness (%)" to set how close a color must be to be selected. In "Sample from", choose "All layers" or "Current layer". In "Selection mode", choose "New", "Add" or "Subtract", then click "Choose".

docs.h: Fill with one color and change colors in bulk
docs.x: These are three items in the "Edit" menu. They affect the inside of the selection if there is one, or the whole selected layer if not. Item Key What it does Fill with foreground color Alt+Backspace Fills with the foreground color Fill with background color Ctrl+Backspace Fills with the background color Change to foreground color (keep transparency) — Changes only the color of painted areas to the current foreground color. The density (transparency) and transparent areas stay as they are "Change to foreground color" is for changing the color of line art in bulk. It is also in the right-click menu of a layer row. When you are painting on a mask, the mask is filled according to the brightness of the color (white = show, black = hide). Inside a normal map folder, it changes colors using gray. It can't be used on normal map image layers (Paint target).

docs.x: Click a drawing on the 3D model and drag to move it. You don't have to look for the layer you drew on: the layer at the point you click is selected. Select the "Move/transform" tool (V). In the 3D view (or UV view), click the drawing you want to move. The topmost layer painted at that point is selected, and a frame appears around its artwork. Keep holding and drag, and it moves right away. Drag a corner to resize and the circle on top to rotate. Press Enter, or switch to another tool, to apply. Press Esc to cancel.

docs.x: Turn off "Auto-select layer" in tool properties to move the selected layer instead of the layer at the point you click. Clicking outside the frame applies the move and switches to the layer at the point you clicked. If a selection exists, only the inside of it moves. Applying counts as one Undo step. In tool properties, use "Shape" to choose the frame type (Scale/rotate, Free transform or Warp) and "Warp grid" to choose the number of grid points (Free transform and Warp). Clicking a text layer gives you the text frame. Drag inside the frame to move it, and double-click to retype (Retype text).

"No visible layers are painted here" appears: Hidden layers, areas hidden by a mask, and drawings at 0% opacity are not picked. Select the layer in the Layers panel, then turn off "Auto-select layer" and move it. A different layer moves: When layers overlap, the topmost layer is picked. Select the layer you want to move and turn off "Auto-select layer".

Shows a frame for resizing and rotating the artwork inside the selection, or the artwork of the whole layer. The frame appears both on the model in the 3D view and in the UV view. Select the area you want to change (not needed for the whole layer). Choose Edit → "Transform (on 3D/UV)" (Ctrl+T). A frame appears. Drag inside the frame to move, drag a corner to scale, and drag the circle on top to rotate. Press Enter to apply, or Esc to cancel.

docs.x: The image is placed at its original aspect ratio, sized to fit the visible area. Transparent areas stay transparent. Press Esc to cancel, and nothing is left behind. docs.x: Text you paste with "To new layer" turned on becomes a text layer, marked with a "T" in the layer list. Text pasted on the UV is always a text layer. You can change the characters, font, color and so on later and paste it again. In the layer list, double-click the text layer (or right-click → "Retype text"). The text window and frame open in the state they were in when you pasted. The color and size of each character are kept too. Edit the text and press Ctrl+Enter to redraw it. Undo brings back the previous version. You can also start by clicking the text with the Text tool, or with "Retype the selected text layer" in tool properties. For text pasted on 3D, the view first returns to the one you had when you pasted, and then the frame appears. When you finish, the view goes back to what it was. To rename it, right-click → "Rename". Right-click → "Rasterize (text can no longer be edited)" turns it into an ordinary layer. It is saved in the project file, so you can still retype it after reopening. In a PSD, it is written as an ordinary layer.

Pressing a key doesn't change the tool: Shortcuts don't work while you're typing text. Press Esc to stop typing. The painting you added disappeared when you retyped: Once you paint over a text layer, its mark changes to "T+". Retyping discards what you added, so press Ctrl+Z to undo, move your added painting to a separate layer, and then retype. "Font not found" appears: A loaded font can be used only until you quit the app. The text is retyped in another font. To get the original font back, load it again with "Load font". You can't retype it: Text pasted into the current layer with "To new layer" turned off, and text that has been rasterized, are ordinary artwork.

docs.x: Unlike the normal Add and Color dodge, they glow strongly even where you've lowered the opacity or at the soft edges of a soft brush. The border follows the shape after the mask is applied. A clipped layer stays within the painted area of its base. You can add it to folders (the combined shape of the contents) and text layers (it stays even if you retype the text). Merge down and Merge folder bake the stroke before merging. It's stored in the project file along with its values. PNG and material exports use the picture with the stroke, and in a PSD it becomes a layer with the stroke baked into pixels (PSD). Other effects added in an earlier version or in a PSD (such as drop shadow) open looking exactly as before. You can't change them, but you can use "Bake into pixels" or "Remove" in the layer properties. Adding, changing and pasting strokes requires Standard. Even in Lite, the strokes in project files you open look as they did, and you can show, hide, copy, clear and bake them into pixels.

The border is cut off at an island edge or spills onto the next island: Strokes are calculated on the UV. Parts that go past the island edge may look cut off at the island edge in 3D. On export, the parts outside the island are handled the same way as padding.

Stacks a brightness or color correction over the picture below without rewriting it. You can change the values any time. Select the layer just above the picture you want to correct. Click the "Adjust" button in the panel and choose a type. An adjustment layer is created. Move the values in the Layer properties panel. While you drag, only the picture changes, and when you release, it counts as one step you can undo. There are 15 types: Hue/Saturation/Lightness, Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Invert, Grayscale, Posterize, Threshold, Gradation map, Curves, Color Balance, Exposure, Color Temperature, Vibrance, Replace Color and Add noise. The values are the same as for Filters. An adjustment layer applies to everything visible below it. You can limit where it applies with a mask. When you select an adjustment layer, the draw-on target is the mask. "Create mask from selection" can replace the current mask. With clipping on, it applies only to the layer just below it. "Merge with layer below" bakes the correction into the pixels of the layer below. In a PSD, Curves, Color Balance, Vibrance, Exposure and Gradation map are exported and imported as adjustment layers. In Lite, you can see the values of adjustment layers in project files you open, but you can't change them (a lock icon appears). Features that read the surrounding picture, such as Blur, Sharpen and Mosaic, don't become adjustment layers (they would be too heavy). Apply them as filters.

You can undo mistakes with Undo (Ctrl+Z). With the History panel, you can go back several steps at once. To do this How Undo one step Undo (Ctrl+Z; hold it down to keep undoing) Redo what you undid Redo (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z) Go back or forward several steps Click a row in the "History" panel. You go back or forward at once to the state after that operation History lists the operations so far, oldest first. ▶ marks the current position, and dimmed rows are operations you can redo. Up to 30 steps are recorded, and the oldest are dropped first. Show or hide the panel from Display → Windows.
