docs.x: Operations that change the picture (layers, masks, paint targets, material settings) can be undone. Operations that change only how things look, and app settings, are not recorded in Undo. Not recorded: turning a texture set's visibility on or off, Visible area (hide, show selected only, show all), object visibility, blend shapes, the view, shading, the mesh wireframe, adding and reordering color sets, sub tools, settings and key bindings. A layer's visibility is part of the picture, so it can be undone. "Hide selected" (H) records only the part of the selection that gets deselected, as one step. To bring back hidden areas, use "Show all" (Alt+H) (Visible area). Right after hiding, the first Ctrl+Z only gives you a notice, and pressing it again undoes the painting before that. Deleting a color set swatch can be undone. These operations can't be undone, so a confirmation appears first: deleting a sub tool, deleting a color set, resetting key bindings, and resetting the brush size list. Changing the texture resolution clears the whole Undo history.

So that stacking lots of 4096-resolution layers doesn't make things slow, layers you haven't touched for a while are taken out of GPU memory and kept elsewhere. The look, export and saving are unchanged. The GPU holds only the selected layer, the combined picture of everything below it, and the combined picture of everything above it. Other layers are shrunk and kept one at a time while you're not drawing on them (areas you haven't painted aren't kept). Selecting, drawing on, undoing, merging or exporting a resting layer brings it back on the spot. With selections that reload many layers, "Preparing…" appears and then it switches (about 0.1 to 0.3 seconds for 80 layers at 4096). If there are layers above with a blend mode other than Normal, or adjustment layers, those stay in the GPU. Layers also stay resting when you open a project file. To turn it off, use File → Preferences → Painting → Performance, "Rest layers you aren't drawing on" (on by default). When it's off, all layers are kept in the GPU. There's also a mechanism that rests whole texture sets you haven't selected (Texture set memory savings).

docs.x: Use Filters → "Create padding on a new layer" to put only the extra area onto a new layer. Pixels outside the islands take the color of the nearest island pixel by straight-line distance, so the color spreads smoothly even from diagonal edges.

Select islands or faces in the UV pane or in 3D (with the Selection tool's "Select by island" or "Select by face", the lasso, vertex groups and so on). Press Shift+H (or use the Visible area icon at the top left of the 3D view, or "Show selected only" in the UV header). Only what you selected appears in 3D. Press it again to show everything Hide selected (H) Hides the selected islands or faces. Hiding releases the selection, so you can paint straight on what is visible Also show selected Brings the selected part of what you hid back into view Invert visible area Swaps what is visible with what is hidden Expand, Contract Expands or contracts the visible area on the UV by the number of px you set (1 to 64) Show all (Alt+H) Brings back everything you hid, including hidden objects All of these are in Display → Visible area, and in the "Visible area" item of the 3D and UV right-click menus. You can restore a selection that was released with "Reselect" in the bar under the 3D view, or with Ctrl+Shift+D. Hidden areas show diagonal stripes in the UV pane. While something is hidden, "Show all" is highlighted. You can also hide by object (mesh) (Show or hide objects).

Choose "Hide pen" in the toolbar on the left (you can also toggle it with "Hide pen" in the bar under the 3D view). In the Sub tool, choose "Hide by face" (a quad is hidden as its two triangles together) or "Hide by island" (a whole UV island: one piece of cloth, one part and so on). docs.h: Paint along UV edges (Paint from UV edges)
docs.x: Creates a line or gradient on a new layer based on the distance from the edges of UV islands. Use it for trim along clothing edges, or for painting that is darker toward the edges. docs.h: UV orientation for glTF, glb and VRM
docs.x: glTF counts the top and bottom of an image the opposite way from FBX and similar formats. When PetaNuri3D opens a glTF, glb or VRM, it flips the UV vertically so that it matches FBX. The picture in the UV pane, exported PNGs, PSDs and UV maps have the same orientation as the original image. They line up as they are in other 3D software. docs.h: Choose the set to draw on
docs.x: You can paint on the selected texture set. Normally you don't need to select it again, because PetaNuri3D switches automatically to the set where you start drawing. You can also choose from "Texture set" in the right-click menu of the UV pane. When you select a set again, that set glows softly in 3D and then fades, so you can see which area belongs to it. While a set that was resting wakes up, "Switching texture set…" appears (about 0.2 seconds at 2048, about 0.5 to 1.5 seconds at 4096). Pen movement during that time is remembered and painted once the set is awake, so lines are not cut off. Undo and redo keep working after you change sets. If you undo an operation on another set, that set becomes selected. The Layers panel and the UV pane show the layers and UV of the selected set.

You can paint both sets in one continuous stroke. Two sets stay awake and paintable: the selected set (Main) and the set you selected before it (Sub). Their names appear at the bottom left of the 3D view, and clicking Sub swaps it with Main. In the panel, the Main row is pink and the Sub row is blue, each with a badge. Each set is painted on the layer selected in that set. A single undo reverts both. The brush circle does not spill onto a set that the pen tip is not on. If you draw the eyes, the skin is not painted too. The same goes for Blur, Smudge, Blend and Liquify. In the UV pane, you paint only on the Main set. docs.h: Hide a set and show it as pixels
docs.x: In the 3D display, this shows the texture as square pixels, one at a time, without interpolation. It is meant for low-resolution textures such as 32 px or 64 px. In the row's right-click menu ("…"), click "Show as pixels (no interpolation)". A small square icon appears to the right of the name. Click the icon to turn it off. Sets of 256 px or less have it on from the start (automatic). A set you have turned on or off yourself keeps that choice in the project file. "Reset pixel display to automatic (on for 256px or less)" undoes the choices you made yourself. To switch all sets at once, use Display → Shading → "Show all sets' textures as pixels (no interpolation)". This only changes the display. Your painting and exports don't change. docs.h: Hide objects or show only one
docs.x: The "Objects" panel on the right lists the model's objects (meshes such as hair, clothing and props). You can use it, for example, to hide a whole piece of clothing and paint the body underneath. In the Objects panel, click the eye button of the object you want to hide. It disappears from 3D. To show only that object, hold Alt while you click its eye button or name (hold Alt and click again to show everything). To bring them back, click "Show all" at the top of the panel or press Alt+H. If the original has a hierarchy, it is shown indented. Each row has an eye button, the name and a badge for the texture set it uses. Click a name to make that object glow briefly in 3D. Click a badge to select that texture set. Row right-click: Show only this, Hide / Show, Highlight in 3D, Show all. The 3D right-click menu also has "Hide this object" and "Show only this object". Hidden objects don't appear in 3D, can't be hit by a click, and aren't painted. The same goes for Also paint back and hidden faces, the opposite side of Symmetry, Fill, Gradient and Stamp. Whatever lies behind a hidden object is visible and paintable as it is. The textures (layers) remain. Exports of PNG, PSD and materials don't change either. While objects are hidden, the bar under the 3D view shows "n object(s) hidden" and "Show all". Show all (Alt+H) restores both the visible area and the objects (Visible area). The hidden state is saved in the project file. Hiding and showing are not recorded in the undo history. With "Give only this object a separate material" and "Assign material" in the row's right-click menu, you can split materials by object (split materials).

Click "Load" to apply that state (a single undo reverts it). "Overwrite" replaces it with the current state, you can rename it in the name field, and × deletes it. You can store up to 10, and they are saved in the project file. The same list also appears in the Blend shapes panel.

docs.h: Save GPU memory (when it is slow)
docs.x: Textures use GPU memory (VRAM). With 4096 sets or many layers it can run out, which makes things slow or stops you from painting. PetaNuri3D frees memory by letting items you aren't using go to sleep.

docs.h: Save GPU memory (when it is slow)
docs.x: Sets you haven't selected are put to sleep, which frees GPU memory without changing how they look. Only two are awake: the Main and the Sub. When you select a sleeping set, you can paint after about 0.2 seconds at 2048 or about 0.5 to 1.5 seconds at 4096. If you click a sleeping 4096 set in the panel, "Preparing…" appears. Saving, PNG/PSD export, AO and filters that apply to all sets work on sleeping sets as they are. Layers you haven't touched for a while are also kept in a shrunken form while you aren't drawing (File → Preferences → Painting → Performance, "Rest layers you aren't drawing on", on by default). Appearance, export and saving don't change (Rest layers). You can see the current amount in the "GPU memory estimate" at the top of the Texture sets panel and in the numbers on each row.

docs.h: Save GPU memory (when it is slow)
docs.x: Check the GPU memory estimate at the top of the Texture sets panel. As a guide, you need at least 4 GB of GPU memory to paint at 2048 and at least 8 GB for 4096 (System requirements). Close other apps that use the GPU, such as games, browsers and video. Lower the resolution of sets that don't need that much detail (Change the resolution). If you aren't painting across sets, remove the Sub to let it sleep (Remove sub). If you had turned "Rest layers you aren't drawing on" off, turn it on. "Display processing stopped" appears: The GPU's display processing was restarted, and your painting can no longer be shown. It happens when resuming from sleep or when memory runs out. You can't paint in this state, and nothing is saved. Reopen with "Open from autosave" or "Reopen project file" in the window (your previous project file and autosave are left intact). "Display processing has stopped, so it can't export" appears: Same as above. Reopen, then export. I wait every time I select a set: A sleeping set is being woken up. If you set the two sets you switch between as the Main and the Sub, you won't have to wait.
docs.s: When it is slow or you can't paint

docs.x: Sets for materials that aren't in the current model are kept, marked with !, rather than deleted. You can move the layers you painted to another set. This happens when you reload the model, and when you open a project file that was saved without the model (FBX) together with a model whose names don't match. In the Texture sets panel, click the set that has a !. The "Set not in the model: (set name)" window opens. Choose layers with "Layers to move" (all of them are selected at first; there are also "Select all" and "Deselect all"). Choose a set with "Destination" (a set with a similar name is selected at first). Click "Move". The layers go to the top of the destination's layers, in the same order. Folders, masks, clipping and blend modes are carried over as they are. If the resolution differs, the layers are scaled to the destination size. UV position stays the same. If you check "Also keep in the original set (copy only)", the layers are only copied and also remain in the original set. A set with no layers left disappears. You can also use "Delete this set" in the window to delete it together with the layers you painted. All of these can be undone. The row's right-click menu also has "Move layers to another set" and "Delete this set". A set with a! doesn't appear in 3D and can't be painted on. It is also left out of exporting all sets and of AO. If you need the picture of only that set, use "Export PNG (no bleed outside islands)" or "Export as PSD" in the row's right-click menu.

docs.h: Paint shadow color, masks and bump (paint targets)
docs.x: Button What it does White, Gray, Black Switches the foreground color. For paint targets that read only brightness (masks, Shadow AO, normal map, outline width), you paint by brightness even if you pick a color. When you go back to color, the previous foreground color returns Fill all Fills the whole layer you are drawing on inside the folder with the foreground color Show only this Shows only the image of that paint target Clear Deletes the folder with its contents and returns to the unpainted state (undo with Ctrl+Z) Back to color Returns to normal color painting (you can also use Edit → "Set paint target back to color") Inside the folder it works like ordinary layers: you can add, delete and reorder layers, and use opacity, blend mode, mask, clipping, Stroke and Merge down. The image made by stacking the layers inside is the image for that paint target. Only the paint targets in use get folders. You can't move or delete the folder itself (to remove it, use "Clear"). Layers inside the folder don't count toward Lite's layer limit. Areas you erase with the eraser return to the unpainted state. The UV pane also shows the image of the paint target you are painting.
docs.s: The top center bar while painting

docs.h: Paint shadow color, masks and bump (paint targets)
docs.x: In the "Material" panel under "Normal map", turn on "Use normal map". Click "Normal map" under "Paint:". A "Normal map" folder is created at the top of the layers. Raise with white and carve with black. Blur softens it. You can change the strength later with "Normal map strength". Normal map images made in other software: Use "Add normal map image", or select a layer inside the folder and drop the image onto the window. It goes in as normals, not as height (the layer gets a "Normal" badge). For an image with DirectX orientation, turn on "DirectX orientation (green flipped)" in Layer properties. Add texture from a pattern: Lay down patterns such as knit, denim, canvas and herringbone as repeating bump. Change the size, rotation and seams with "Repeating pattern" in Layer properties. You can decide where it applies with a mask. While a layer inside the folder is selected, the UV pane shows the normal map's color (blue-violet) instead of the height (gray). To switch back to gray, use right-click → Display → "Show the normal map folder as height (gray) (UV)". There is also a tool for drawing bump (Bump). When you export, PNG gives a single <name>_normal.png, and PSD keeps the layers separate inside a "Normal map" group.

docs.h: Paint shadow color, masks and bump (paint targets)
docs.x: "Can't add any more" appears: A single material can use at most 16 textures at once in the Final look display. Turn off other features, or "Clear" paint targets you don't use, and then you can use it. I pick a color but can only paint gray: You are painting a paint target that reads only brightness. To go back to normal colors, click "Back to color". I can't delete or move a paint target folder: Folders can't be deleted. To remove a whole paint target, click "Clear" at the top center.

You can paint the images for lilToon's "Main color 2nd" and "Main color 3rd" separately from the main image. Use it when you want to layer a design or pattern from another image. In the "Material" panel under "Main color 2nd", turn on "Use Main color 2nd". A "Main color 2nd" folder is created at the top of the Layers panel. Select the folder, then add layers and paint. You can also drag ordinary layers into it. Set how it overlaps (color, opacity, blend mode, apply light brightness) in the panel. Only the layers inside the folder become the 2nd (3rd) texture, and they don't mix into the main image. The blend modes are Normal, Add, Screen and Multiply. With the paint target "Main color 2nd mask", you can paint where it overlaps (white) and where it doesn't (black). The folder can't be moved, deleted or duplicated. While it contains layers, you can't turn off "On" (if you empty it, you can turn it off, and the folder goes away too). On export, they become separate images (<name>_main2nd.png, <name>_main3rd.png, and the masks you painted). In PSD they stay as a folder, and when you import it again it returns to this folder. In the material, they go into lilToon's "Main color 2nd/3rd".

docs.h: Change settings for only some objects (split materials)
docs.x: You can change settings such as shadow color, MatCap, rim light and outline for each object while keeping the same texture (the image you paint). For example, with the hair texture unchanged, you can make only the animal ears' shadows red. In the 3D view, right-click the object, or right-click its row in the Objects panel. Choose "Give only this object a separate material". A copy of the current material is added under the object's name and assigned to it. In the "Material" panel, change the settings of that material. At first, each texture set has one material with the same name. If you don't split, nothing changes. With "Assign material" in the right-click menu, or "Assign to object" in the panel, you can choose which material to use. You can choose only materials that use the same texture set. In the list at the top of the panel, you can add (a copy of the current material), rename, delete, and move up or down. The texture set's original material can't be deleted. The order of the list is the priority. When objects overlap at the same spot, the upper material is chosen. The panel switches to the material of the spot you touch in 3D, and the status bar below shows "Material: name (texture set name)". On export, there is one .mat per material. The textures are one set per texture set, and the materials point to the same ones.

docs.x: You can load a lilToon material that comes with an avatar and keep painting from its settings and images. When you export, only the parts you repainted are written back into the original material. Choose File → Import → "Load lilToon material (.mat, .unitypackage)". Choose a .mat, or a .unitypackage that contains one. You can also drop it onto the window. If you chose several, check the texture sets they will go into in the window that appears (they go into the set with the matching name). If any textures can't be found, they are listed so you can choose the images (if you don't, they are loaded without them). You can also choose it under "Start with" on the New screen (Types of starting point). Settings that come in: rendering mode, render face, Main color, shadow, normal map, MatCap/2nd, rim light, backlight, rim shade, emission, outline, Main color 2nd/3rd and more. Images that come in: Main color goes to the base layer (every layer, if it is a PSD); 2nd/3rd go to their folders; shadow colors, masks, rim light color, emission, outline width and AO go to paint targets; MatCap goes to MatCap; and the normal map goes to the Normal map folder (as normals). Textures are searched for in the project (Assets, Packages) that contains the .mat. The first time takes several seconds to over ten seconds. For a .unitypackage, it searches inside the package. If you choose several .mat files that use the same texture, they go into the same texture set, and from the second one on they become separate materials. Loading can be undone (one step). That set's material settings, paint targets, base image and Main color 2nd/3rd are replaced.

docs.x: Settings that PetaNuri3D doesn't imitate (stencil, distance fade, UV animation, texture tiling and so on) are listed in "Unreproduced settings" after you load. The values stay as they are and go back unchanged when you export. You can also see the list from the "lilToon: (name).mat" section of the panel.

When you export a loaded material, only the lines for the settings you changed and the textures you repainted are rewritten, in the same place and with the same ID as the original .mat. Textures you didn't change are not exported. If you import the .unitypackage into the project, the original materials and textures are overwritten in place (assignments to the model stay). If you repaint a texture that was not a PNG or was not found, a new PNG is created next to the .mat and swapped in. To export as a new material, click "Unlink from source" in the panel. This overwrites files in the original project. If you don't want to rewrite the materials of an avatar you bought directly, copy the project first, or click "Unlink from source" before you export.
docs.s: Write back to the original material

docs.h: Export materials and hand them to Unity
docs.x: Exports the lilToon materials (.mat) together with the images you painted. When you import it into Unity, you get materials with the textures already assigned. Choose File → Export → "Export materials (.unitypackage / folder)" (or "Export materials" in the "Material" panel). Check "Materials to export". Set "Destination folder name (under Assets)", the resolution and "Padding". Click "Export to .unitypackage" and choose where to save. In Unity, double-click the resulting .unitypackage, or drag it into the Project window, to import it. What goes in: materials (.mat) and images such as Main color, shadow color, masks, normal map and MatCap. Paint targets are included only while that feature is in use. "Export to folder": If you choose the Assets folder of a Unity project, it writes directly with .meta files (app (exe) only). Images have their color spread outside the islands by the width of "Padding" (export bleed). If you export the same work again with the same folder name, what you imported before is overwritten in place (assignments to the model stay). Sets with a! (sets that aren't in the model) are not exported. What is exported is a material for lilToon (2.3 series). Make sure lilToon is installed in the project you import into.

docs.h: Export materials and hand them to Unity
docs.x: The material turns pink in Unity: lilToon isn't installed in that project. Installing lilToon fixes it. "Export to folder" isn't available: It works only in the app (exe). Export to .unitypackage instead. It doesn't show on the avatar: Assign the exported material in the model's material slots. If you loaded an original .mat and exported it, the original material is overwritten in place.

This creates a picture in which the areas light can hardly reach are darkened, based on the shape of the model. Use it as a base for shading or when you want to add depth. Open Filters → Bake → "Bake AO (areas darkened by surroundings)". In the "Texture sets to bake" table, check the sets you want to bake. At first, the visible sets are checked. Choose "Quality" and "Shadow distance". If you're unsure, leave the defaults. Click "Bake". An "AO" layer in Multiply mode is added at the top of each set. Close the window with "Close" or ×. You can still move the 3D view while baking. If you stop with "Cancel", nothing changes. One Undo restores all sets. Estimated time: about 30 seconds for an avatar with 6 texture sets at 2048 resolution, with the default settings (when calculated on the GPU). For sets whose rendering mode is "Cutout" or "Transparent", light passes through the transparent parts of the picture (such as hair tips). "Opaque" ignores transparency (see Rendering mode).
docs.k: ambient occlusion crevices contact shadows darken gaps occlusion map baking shading

docs.x: Column Meaning Bake Bakes AO into this set's texture (it receives shadows from other objects) Cast shadows This set also casts shadows onto other sets. If you uncheck it, it casts shadows only onto itself Ignore other shadows Does not receive shadows from other sets. Check this when something that is covered, such as the body under clothing, turns pitch black For example, if you bake the body and set the hair and clothing to "Cast shadows" only, the shadows of the hair and clothing fall on the body.
docs.s: Table of texture sets to bake

docs.x: Item Options Rays 64 to 4096 per texel (512 by default). More rays remove graininess but take longer Within texel 1×1 (center only, fast), 2×2, 4×4 (checks 16 spots, so edges are smooth; default) Distance Near (3 cm; only where surfaces touch, such as between fingers, collars and hairlines), Normal (8 cm; also under bangs, armpits, under the chin and skirt hems; default), Wide (20 cm; more realistic, so an arm also darkens the side of the body), Custom (the value in cm below) Scale to the model's height (distance for a 1.5 m tall model) Makes the distance proportional to the model's height. The distance that actually applies is shown in the window

The body under the clothing turns pitch black: Check "Ignore other shadows" on the body's set and bake again. Grain (noise) is noticeable: Increase "Rays", or set "Within texel" to 4×4. "Dither" in the detailed settings also makes the steps in the gradation less visible. No light passes through the hair tips: Set the hair material's rendering mode to "Cutout" or "Transparent", then bake. It isn't in the menu, or it has a lock icon: This is a Pro feature.

In the "Objects" section of the dialog, you can choose what to bake per object (mesh). For example, with the sample "Shinobu", choosing only furin bakes only the bell. In the "Objects" section, click "None" to uncheck everything. Check the objects you want to bake. Click a name to make it glow slightly in 3D. Choose how shadows are calculated, then click "Bake". It writes only to the UV area of the selected objects (and a little beyond the islands). The areas of other objects in the same texture set stay as they are. "Shadows from selected only" (default): calculates with only the shape of the selected objects. Shadows from other things, such as the body, are not included. "Shadows from whole model": objects you didn't select also cast shadows. Areas close to the body get darker. Sets that contain none of the selected objects are not baked. If all objects are selected, the whole model is baked. Your selection is remembered per model.

docs.x: If the baked AO is too dark or too light, you can adjust it either after or before baking. After baking: Lower the opacity of the "AO" layer. You can also use a mask or the Eraser to remove only the areas you don't need. Before baking: Change the darkness with "Strength" (0 gives white) and "Contrast" under "Final look". Use "Reset to defaults" to return the settings to their initial values (your choice of sets stays as it is).

docs.x: Item Details Falloff Smooth (farther hits count less; default), Linear, None (same strength within the distance) Normal Smooth (around the interpolated normal; default), Surface orientation Compute Auto (GPU, or CPU if unavailable), CUDA (NVIDIA GPU; app (exe) only, experimental), CPU (very slow) Verify GPU results on the CPU Checks a small sample of the calculation results for each set Meshes not in any set also cast shadows Meshes that can't be painted (such as those with no UV) are also counted as objects that cast shadows Outside islands The width (px) to extend outside the islands. If you choose "Auto", it is decided for you Fill everything outside islands Keeps the background from mixing into the edges even when the texture is shrunk Dither Makes the steps in smooth gradations less visible Offset from surface The distance the starting point of each check is raised off the surface (mm, for a 1.5 m tall model) Nearby translucency Translucent surfaces within this many mm are ignored (thin meshes such as cheek blush) To make the white areas of the AO transparent and change the shadow color, you can use Convert luminance to opacity. To add soft shading based on surface orientation, or cast shadows from light, go to Easy Bake, material look and shading.

docs.h: Output as lilToon Shadow AO or PNG
docs.x: In the "Export" section of the dialog, you can choose where the baked AO goes. You can choose any number of them. Item Where it goes Add an "AO" layer (Multiply, top of the set) Bakes into the texture color (default) Also write to lilToon's "Shadow AO" (AO Map) Adds the AO layer to the top of the material's "Shadow AO" paint target folder. The darker an area is, the more easily shadow appears there. It is output together with the Material export Also save as PNG after baking (<set name>_AO.png) Saves an image of the AO alone You can also save it later from Filters → Bake → "Export AO as PNG (last bake result)". Areas outside the islands are filled using the extension width in the AO settings (or the export bleed, if that is wider). When writing to Shadow AO, if that set isn't using shadows, it is switched to "Use shadow" (Undo reverts this). lilToon's AO map shifts the shadow boundary. If the shadow feels too strong, bake again with "Strength" at 0.6 to 0.8.

docs.h: Create a base coat with Easy Bake
docs.x: Easy Bake bakes shading and gloss suited to skin, clothing or props into layers all at once. It uses the base color and the original texture as the foundation and layers the effects on top. In the Texture sets panel, select the set to bake. Open Filters → "Easy Bake". Under "Finish", choose skin, clothing, props or another type. The 3D view shows how it will look after baking. Adjust "Overall strength", "Light horizontal angle", "Light elevation" and "Highlight amount". For skin, set where to add blush if you need it. Click "Bake into a layer folder". A folder named after the finish is created, containing one layer per effect and a transparent "Paint details" layer.

Shown only for finishes that include weave or color variation Blush strength / Blush spread Shown only for skin finishes (Add blush) Preview Updates the look in the 3D view every time you change a value Apply to all visible texture sets Bakes the same finish onto every visible set

docs.h: Create a base coat with Easy Bake
docs.x: On the New screen, check "Open Easy Bake after creation" and choose the target set. After the model opens, the Easy Bake window appears. It is unchecked by default. You can set the base color first and then try the finishes (New). The preview is shown on a temporary layer. Click "Cancel" or the × on the window to close it without changing anything. After you confirm, a single undo removes the whole folder.

Each finish has its own set of effects (layers). All of them keep the original colors and layer the effects on top. Finish Layers it contains Skin | Fair and rosy Soft shadow, cavity depth, overall tint, soft highlights Skin | Warm blush Soft shadow, cavity depth, overall tint, soft highlights Skin | Soft illustration Soft shadow, cavity depth, soft highlights (all subtle) Skin | Deeper shading Soft shadow, cavity depth, soft highlights (darker shadows) Clothing | Soft fabric Soft shadow, cavity depth, surface detail (weave) Clothing | Satin style Soft shadow, cavity depth, soft highlights, rim light Clothing | Denim style Soft shadow, cavity depth, surface detail (weave) Clothing | Leather style Soft shadow, cavity depth, surface detail (color variation), soft highlights Clothing | Soft color variation Soft shadow, surface detail (color variation), soft highlights Props | Hard surface Soft shadow, cavity depth, soft highlights (pronounced), rim light General | Warm light Soft shadow, soft highlights, rim light (warm color) General | Blue rim light Soft shadow, rim light (blue) Every folder has a transparent "Paint details" layer at the top. If you place blush locations with a skin finish, a "Blush at selected points" layer is also added. "Overall tint" uses Multiply. The other layers use Normal blending. If you want the skin color to match the face, match the base color first. It is easier to adjust if you start with a light bake.

docs.h: Add blush to cheeks and knees
docs.x: With a skin finish, you can place the spots where you want redness yourself. A soft red tint spreads around each point. Choose a skin finish, then click "Add a location" under "Where to add blush". In the 3D view, click where you want redness, such as a cheek, elbow or knee. To move a point, drag the move handle in the 3D view or type the X, Y and Z coordinates. Adjust "Blush strength" and "Blush spread" while keeping the fair skin tone. When you bake, the blush becomes a separate layer named "Blush at selected points". You can add as many locations as you like (up to 16). To remove a point, select it in the list and click "Remove selected location". If you turn on "Add blush symmetrically", the same amount of blush is added on the opposite side. The center is the same as the center of Symmetry (X) used when painting. If you move the original point, the opposite one follows. It is off by default. "Blush spread" is a ratio of the model's height. This does not find cheeks or knees automatically. If you place no points, no per-location blush is added.

docs.h: Bake one effect at a time (Bake)
docs.x: Filters → Bake lists a bake command for each effect. You can bake just the effect you want to add after Easy Bake onto a new layer. Select the texture set to bake. Choose the effect you want from Filters → Bake. Pick a similar look from "Presets" and adjust the values. The 3D view shows the look immediately. Click "Bake to a new layer". A new layer is added to the selected set. Bake menu item What it bakes Bake AO (areas darkened by surroundings) Dark crevices (Bake AO) Export AO as PNG (last bake result) (Output AO as PNG) Bake cast shadows Shadows cast by hair and clothes (cast shadows) Bake thin-surface tint Translucent tint in thin areas such as ears and fingers (translucent tint) Bake soft shading Soft shadows based on face orientation (shading) Bake gradients by orientation, height or point Colors that change with face orientation, height or distance from a point (gradients) Bake rim light / Bake gloss highlights / Bake weave and color variation Rim light, gloss, weave and color variation (material look) Bake toon shade (1st, 2nd) Crisp two-step shadows (toon shade) Bake angel ring (hair highlight) Ring highlight on hair (angel ring) Enhance cavities and bulges Shadows in cavities and brightness on bulges (cavities and bulges) If you turn on "Apply to all visible texture sets", the effect is baked onto every visible set. If there is a selection, only the inside of it is baked (only sets that have a selection are targeted). You can rotate the view to check even during the preview. Click "Cancel" or the × on the window to close it without changing anything. The preview is shown at a low resolution and is rebuilt at the set's resolution when you confirm. Check how fine weave and shading look after confirming too. Cast shadows, thin-surface tint and AO are calculated after you choose the targets and quality. A progress display appears, and you can cancel partway. What gets baked is texture color. Moving the view, or a light in Unity, after baking does not move the painted light or shadows. To check only the base color, set Shading to "Unlit (painted colors)".

With "Pick center in 3D view", you can place the point on the surface of the model or in empty space. docs.h: Bake cast shadows and thin-surface tint
docs.x: Creates shadows cast by hair and clothes from the overlaps in the current pose. You can use them together with shading layers. Open Filters → Bake → "Bake cast shadows". Set Light horizontal angle, Light elevation, Shadow softness, Shadow strength, Shadow color, Shadow distance (cm) and Quality. For each texture set, choose "Receive shadows" or "Cast shadows". For example, you can bake shadows onto the body and have hair and clothes only cast shadows. Click "Bake to a new layer".

docs.h: Bake cast shadows and thin-surface tint
docs.x: Probes inward from each face and adds color to thin spots where the opposite face is close by. It adds a soft translucent tint to closed shapes such as ears and fingers, and to thin props. Open Filters → Bake → "Bake thin-surface tint". Set "Thinness range (cm)", "Tint strength", "Translucent tint" and "Quality". Check "Bake" for the sets to bake, then click "Bake to a new layer". A single open sheet of cloth is not a target for the translucent tint. If there is another face on the inside, it also picks up the distance to that face, so check the result and adjust the strength. This is not a material setting that actually lets light pass through.

Baked effects are ordinary paint layers. You can change their strength and range later. You can lower a layer's opacity, hide effects you don't need, narrow the range with a mask, or erase parts with the eraser. Easy Bake puts each effect on its own layer. This lets you, for example, weaken the shadows and keep only the blush. If you paint on the "Paint details" layer, you can keep painting without disturbing the baked effects. You can undo a bake with Ctrl+Z. If you save to a project file (.petanuri), the baked layers are kept as they are. PNG exports the visible effects merged into one image, and PSD exports with the layers kept separate (Export).

docs.x: Shadows are doubled or too dark: Baking again adds new layers. Hide or delete the old effect layers and compare. Shadows don't move when I rotate the view: Baked shadows are texture color, so they don't move. To see shadows that move with the light, use the Final look display. I can't confirm the distance-from-point gradient: Place a point with "Pick center in 3D view", then bake. No blush is added: With a skin finish, click "Add a location" and place a point. If there are no points, no per-location blush is added. The pattern detail differs between the preview and the result: The preview uses a low resolution. Adjust it by how it looks after confirming. docs.h: Pose the model and paint in that shape
docs.x: Use this to paint spots that are hard to draw in a T-pose, such as the armpits and the inside of the arms. If you lower the arms first, the pen reaches more easily. Click "Pose" at the top center of the 3D view. You can't draw while in Pose mode. Click the joint dot of the bone you want to move. If you click the mesh, the bone that moves that spot the most is selected. Drag the gizmo that appears to rotate the bone. Click "Paint" to go back. The paint positions are rebuilt in the posed shape, and you can paint right away. Other ways in: Display → Mode & pose → "Pose mode (move bones)", or right-click in the 3D view → "Enter pose mode (move bones)". In the key bindings, you can assign a key to "Toggle paint/pose" (Assign keys). The pose is saved in the project file. You can combine it with blend shapes.

docs.x: In "Pose presets" at the bottom of the "Pose" panel, click "Save current state". The current pose is remembered with a name (up to 10). Change the name in the name field and press Enter. To use it, click "Load". Bones that weren't saved go back to their original pose. "Overwrite" replaces a preset with the current pose, and × deletes it. One Undo reverts a load. Presets are stored in the project file. If you paint with symmetry while posed, strokes land at the symmetric spot in the original pose. The bone lines between body parts are orange too Green Fingers Blue, smaller Everything else (swaying parts such as hair, skirt, chest and tail) If there's a humanoid bone near where you click, it's selected before other bones. The list in the "Pose" panel gets the same color marks. Turn on "Humanoid only" to hide the swaying parts and show only the body and hands. Whether a bone is humanoid is judged by its name. "Mirror L→R" and "Mirror R→L": Copy the pose of one side to the other side. Left and right are the character's left and right. One Undo reverts it. You can use them from the top center row (Symmetry, L→R, R→L), the "Pose" panel, the right-click menu and Display → Mode & pose. Left/right pairs are decided by name (Left/Right, .L/.R, _L/_R, a trailing L/R and so on). If the names don't tell, bones at mirrored positions in the original pose are paired.

docs.x: You can paint with the model's blend shapes (shape keys) applied. Use this to paint spots that can't be seen in the original shape, such as closed eyes or the inside of the mouth. Open the "Blend shapes" panel on the right. If there are two or more meshes, choose a mesh from the dropdown at the top ("All meshes" is also available). Move a slider (0 to 100). When you stop, the paint positions are rebuilt in that shape. Paint as usual. Display, painting and hit testing all work in that shape. Use "Filter" to find a name, and "Non-zero only" to show just the shapes you've moved. "All to 0" resets everything. The values are saved in the project file.

docs.x: Turns the picture of each texture set into one PNG per set. This is the image you apply to the model in Unity and so on. Choose File → Export → Export PNG (all sets). To export just one set, choose "Export PNG (selected set)" instead. In the export window, check "Resolution", "Padding" and "Destination", then click "Export". If you are asked where to save, choose a folder. For all sets, you choose the folder only once. A message "Exported (name)" appears, and the folder you exported to opens in Explorer.

docs.x: File name What it is <set name>.png The picture made by stacking the visible layers. The set name is the material name <set name>_main2nd.png, <set name>_main3rd.png For sets that have a Main color 2nd/3rd folder. If you painted their masks, files ending in _mask are exported too (Main color 2nd and 3rd) <set name>_normal.png For sets that have a normal map folder as a paint target (Paint targets) Sets that would get the same name are told apart with _2, _3 and so on. Sets whose display is turned off are included in "all sets". Orphaned sets (!) are not. When you need one, export it with "Export PNG (no bleed outside islands)" in the right-click menu on its row (Orphaned sets). Effects such as Stroke are exported with the effects applied. Light, shadow and material look baked with Easy Bake and so on are also included, as colors of the visible layers. Textures are exported as they are, even if you have hidden things with the visible area or objects. You can also export a set with "Export as PNG" in the right-click menu on its row in the Texture sets panel.

With "Resolution" in the export window, you can export at a size different from the texture set's resolution. Choose from "Unchanged (texture set resolution)", 512×512, 1024×1024, 2048×2048, 4096×4096 and 8192×8192. Bleed is added at the set's resolution first, and then the image is scaled down or up. This applies to PNG (selected set and all sets), selected layers, UV map and material exports. It does not apply to PSD (always the set's resolution). To change the resolution you paint at, use the Texture sets panel (Change the resolution).

Lines appear at UV seams in the game: The bleed is not wide enough. Increase it beyond 8 px and export again (Bleed). "Can't export while (name) is shown" appears: A transform frame, a filter preview or similar is open. Confirm (Enter) or cancel (Esc) first, then export. "Another read/write operation is in progress" appears: Saving, Autosave or loading is in progress. Wait until it finishes, then try again. "Display processing has stopped, so it can't export" appears: Reopen your project file or an autosave, then export (Memory savings). "No texture set can be exported as PNG" appears: The set you have selected is an orphaned set (!). Select another set, or move its layers, and then export. It says "Export canceled" when I click: You clicked Cancel in the export window or the save window. Values you changed in the window go back as they were.

docs.h: Export only the selected layers as PNG
docs.x: Exports only some layers, such as just the line art or just a pattern, as a PNG with a transparent background. In the Layers panel, select the layers to export (Ctrl/Shift+click to select as many as you like). Choose File → Export → Export as PNG (selected layers). You can also use "Export selected layers as PNG" or "Export this layer as PNG" in a layer's right-click menu. For two or more layers, choose "One by one (a file per layer)" or "Combine into one image" under "Selected layers" in the window, then click "Export". Choice File name One by one <set name>_<layer name>.png Combine into one image <set name>_layers.png (stacked in the panel's order, using each blend mode) The background is transparent. Because the picture contains only what you painted, no bleed is added. It remembers your previous choice. It is not available in 2D painting. Export with "Export PNG (selected set)" instead (Details).

Choose File → Export → Export UV map as PNG (selected set). It is also in the right-click menu on the texture set row. Choose the options below in the window and click "Export". <set name>_uv.png is created. Setting Choices Resolution Unchanged (texture set resolution), 512 to 8192 Line color White, black, foreground color Background Transparent, black, white (if transparent, you can overlay it on a picture in other software) Line width 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 px Island edges "Draw island edges twice as thick" (on by default) Destination Same as other exports (Details) A 2D canvas has no UV, so it cannot be exported. docs.x: Layers, visibility, opacity, blend modes, clipping, Lock transparency, folders, layer masks and color tags (layer colors) are kept. Adjustment layers go in as adjustment layers (a Gradation map keeps its color stops). The "Colorize" option of Hue/Saturation/Lightness is not included. Stroke is written as a layer baked into pixels. Text layers become ordinary layers. A base layer that has only Stroke, Drop shadow or Outer glow, and clipped layers, are written separately as they are. A layer named "(layer name)（効果）" (the Japanese word for "effects") is added above, with only the effects baked in. When there is a fill opacity, an inner effect or the like, everything is merged into one layer. The folders for paint targets, Normal map and Main color 2nd/3rd are written as hidden groups. They are restored when you import into PetaNuri3D. The composite image (the flat picture you get without opening the PSD) gets bleed. The layers themselves stay as you painted them. Adjustment-layer calculations may look slightly different in other apps.

You can import the editable PSD that comes with an avatar and keep painting from it. When you import it, the layers of that set are replaced with the contents of the PSD. Choose File → Import → Import PSD (replace layers). Choose the PSD. It goes into the set whose name matches the file name (body.psd → body). If no set matches, it goes into the selected set. You can also drop a PSD onto the window. If you drop it on a texture set row, it goes into that set (Add images or PSDs). If the size is different, it is scaled to the set's resolution. Folders, masks and supported adjustment layers stay as they are. Blend modes that do not match become "Normal", unsupported adjustment layers are skipped, and a notice appears at the bottom right. One Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings it back. When you create a new project, you can also set the starting point (Base) to "PSD" and import it (Open a 3D model).

Spreads the edge colors outward beyond the UV islands when exporting. Without it, lines may show at UV seams in the game when the texture is scaled down or mipmaps are applied. In the export window, choose the width to spread under "Padding". Click "Export". Value What it does None (don't extend outside islands) Does not spread outside the islands (if a base is visible, you get the base color) 4, 8 (default), 16, 32, 64, 128 px Spreads color outward from the island edges by that width Fill everything outside islands Fills everything outside the islands with the color of the nearest island It applies to PNGs, the composite image of a PSD, and the images from a material export (Main color, shadow color, masks, normal map and all the rest). The layers inside a PSD are not spread. It is not added to PNGs of selected layers or to UV maps. The value is the same as "Padding" at the bottom left of the UV pane. Changing either one changes both. Values you set in 1 px steps in the UV pane also appear in the window (Paint area and padding). A pixel outside an island takes the color of the nearest island pixel, measured in a straight line. Diagonal edges spread smoothly, without stair-steps. The thin, faint edge of a brush stroke is not counted as painted. The color of the opaque areas is spread first, and then the faint areas are laid on top. This makes lines in the base color less likely to appear at seams. The image sent by the Unity link is spread the same way as an exported PNG (Paint from Unity). Before you export, turn on "Padding line" in the UV pane to see how far the color will spread. If you also want to paint by hand outside the islands, set the paint area to "In padding" (Details).

docs.x: Use "Destination" in the export window to export to the same folder every time. It is handy to choose something like the Textures folder of your Unity project. In the export window, choose a folder with "Select folder". Turn on "Export to this folder without asking each time (overwrites files with the same name)". From then on, PNG, PSD, AO and .unitypackage exports are written to that folder without asking where to save. "Remove" goes back to being asked where to save every time you export. Even when you have not chosen a folder, the save window opens at the folder you last exported to. "Open the folder after exporting" is on from the start. When writing finishes, the folder opens in Explorer. Turn it off if you do not need that. While exporting, "Exporting…" is shown and you cannot do anything else until it finishes. For exporting materials to a folder (choose Assets), the window opens at the Assets folder you chose last time. If you cancel in the window, the values you changed in it (padding, destination and so on) go back as they were. When "Export to this folder without asking each time" is on, files with the same name are overwritten without a check.

Supports Unity 2022.3 (the version used for VRChat avatars). It connects only to Unity on the same computer. Only FBX meshes can be painted. docs.x: Open the "unity" folder inside the PetaNuri3D folder. It contains PetaNuri3D-Unity.unitypackage. With your project open in Unity, drag PetaNuri3D-Unity.unitypackage into the Project window (or use Assets → Import Package → Custom Package). Click "Import" in the window that appears. If ぺたぬり3D (PetaNuri3D) appears in the menu bar at the top, the add-on is installed. The add-on is installed in Assets/PetaNuri3D. It works only inside the editor and is not included in the avatar you upload.

docs.x: In Unity, select the avatar in Hierarchy (the object in the scene) or a prefab in Project. In the menu bar, choose ぺたぬり3D → ぺたぬり3D で塗る (PetaNuri3D → Paint with PetaNuri3D). It is also in the right-click menus of Hierarchy and Project. The Unity menu names are in Japanese only. Only the first time, a message "Choose the PetaNuri3D program" appears. Choose PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe in the PetaNuri3D folder. PetaNuri3D starts and shows the model from Unity. Paint as usual. A texture set is made for each material's main texture. Materials that use the same texture share one set, and what you paint shows on all of those materials. The original texture becomes the base as is, and the resolution is the same as the original texture (Lite is limited to 2048). For a material with no texture, you start painting from the material color. Objects hidden in Unity are also hidden in PetaNuri3D (you can show them in the Objects panel). PetaNuri3D launched from Unity is a screen just for painting. The title is "PetaNuri3D — Unity link (avatar name)", and New, Open project file, Recent files, Reload model and Save as are not shown. If you choose "Paint with PetaNuri3D" again, the open PetaNuri3D comes to the front (a second copy is not started). If a lilToon material uses "Main color 2nd" or "Main color 3rd", their images (including PSD), masks, blend modes and colors come in too, and go into those folders in the Layers panel (Main color 2nd and 3rd). They do not come in with Lite or Standard (in Unity, the original 2nd and 3rd still show as they were).

In the Unity menu bar, choose ぺたぬり3D → ぺたぬり3D の窓を開く (PetaNuri3D → Open the PetaNuri3D window) to open a window that lets you check each step from the top as you paint. Section What it does 1. PetaNuri3D program (exe) Shows the current location and whether it can be used. Has "Choose", "Search" and "Show in Explorer" (Choose the location again) 2. What to paint (prefab or scene avatar) Drag a prefab or avatar into the field, or select it and click "Use selection". The number of paintable meshes and the texture sets are shown. If it cannot be painted, the reason is shown too 3. Paint "Paint with PetaNuri3D" and the current status (Not connected, Starting, Connected, Disconnected, Saved, Finished). While you are painting, you also get "Bring PetaNuri3D to front", "Save and show in Unity", "Finish", "Revert and finish" and "Show painted files" 4. Where files go / Settings Where your painting goes (Assets/PetaNuri/), "Open Preferences" and the language switch The add-on version (the same number as PetaNuri3D) appears at the bottom of the window.

docs.x: Closing PetaNuri3D ends the link. If you choose "Save and quit" when you close, your painting is sent to Unity before PetaNuri3D closes. If you painted an avatar in the scene, Unity asks "Keep" or "Revert to original". Even if you choose "Revert to original", the files in Assets/PetaNuri/ remain, so you can pick up where you left off by painting again. You can also go back with Unity's Undo (Ctrl+Z). If you close without ever saving, it reverts to the original look without asking and deletes what it created. If you close Unity first, you are asked "Save and Close", "Keep Open" or "Close Without Saving".

docs.x: Animations that switch materials, such as outfit color changes, point to the original materials. When you use your painting, replace the materials in those animations too. Do not paint the same avatar in two Unity editors at the same time. While Unity reloads scripts (compiling, or the start of Play mode), the link drops for a moment, but it reconnects right away.

docs.x: I painted, but Unity's look does not change: It shows up when you save. Press Ctrl+S in PetaNuri3D or Unity. Nothing starts when I choose "Paint with PetaNuri3D", or an English page opens: The exe you chose is wrong. Use Choose the PetaNuri3D location again and choose PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe in the folder where you extracted the ZIP. "The PetaNuri3D program files (resources.neu) are not next to the selected file" appears: There is no resources.neu next to the exe you chose. Choose the exe in the folder where you extracted the whole ZIP. "The Unity add-on and PetaNuri3D versions don't match" appears: Import the PetaNuri3D-Unity.unitypackage that comes with PetaNuri3D again. To carry Main color 2nd/3rd, you need the add-on of the same version. "All link ports (47360-47369) are in use" appears: Close the other Unity editors and try again. "The selection has no paintable meshes (FBX meshes)" appears: Select a prefab or avatar that has FBX meshes. It still does not connect: Restart both Unity and PetaNuri3D. For details, see Unity連携の使い方.txt (in Japanese) in PetaNuri3D's unity folder.

The Unity add-on remembers the location of the PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe you chose first. If you moved the PetaNuri3D folder, or extracted a new version into a different folder, choose the location again. In the Unity menu bar, choose ぺたぬり3D → ぺたぬり3D の窓を開く (PetaNuri3D → Open the PetaNuri3D window). Click "Choose" under "1. PetaNuri3D program (exe)". Choose PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe inside the "PetaNuri3D" folder in the new location. If "Found." appears below the field, you are done. If "No file at this location" appears, choose again. Click "Search" to look for "PetaNuri3D" folders on the Desktop, in Downloads, in Documents, in Program Files and at the root of each drive. docs.x: Right-click a toolbar button or a sub tool tile. Choose "Assign key". If it already has a key, it appears like "Assign key (current: P)". Press the key you want to use. The previous key is removed and replaced with the one you pressed (Esc cancels). You can also assign keys by right-clicking the header or tab of the Sub tool and Tool properties panels. docs.x: Use this when you move to another PC, or want to keep a backup. Click "Export key bindings" above the key bindings. Your current assignments are saved to a JSON file (PetaNuri3D-keymap.json). Your current assignments are replaced entirely. Actions that aren't in the file get their default keys. Entries for actions that don't exist in this version are not used.

A key does nothing when you press it: While a menu is open, the app's shortcuts don't work. Close the menu, then press the key. You assigned a numpad key and it doesn't work, or it doesn't work from the top row: Numpad digits and top-row digits are different keys. Reassign the one you use. The keys for reload, print and page zoom don't work: Browser shortcuts don't work in PetaNuri3D.

docs.h: Pen pressure is wrong or doesn't work
docs.x: If "Use Windows Ink" is turned off in your pen tablet settings, the pen arrives as a mouse and no pressure comes through. There are two fixes, and either one is enough. Recommended: In your pen tablet driver's settings screen, turn on "Use Windows Ink". Tilt arrives too. If you keep Windows Ink off: Turn on "Read pen pressure directly (WinTab)" in File → Preferences → Pen & input → "Tablet" (off by default). The path becomes "WinTab". If it looks like you are drawing with a pen but pressure isn't arriving, a notice "Pen pressure is not arriving" appears once at the bottom right. It doesn't appear if you are just drawing with a mouse. "Don't show again" stops it from appearing, and "Open preferences" opens Pen & input.

docs.h: Pen pressure is wrong or doesn't work
docs.x: When you turn on "Read pen pressure directly (WinTab)", pressure (and tilt) is read through the WinTab of your pen tablet driver. It replaces pressure only when you draw with the pen close to the screen. Drawing with a mouse is unchanged. The eraser end of the pen works as the eraser too. "Use WinTab pressure for Windows Ink pens too" (on by default): even when the pen arrives via Windows Ink, if WinTab values are arriving, it uses those pressure and tilt values. When it is off, it keeps the Windows Ink pressure. If you use it at the same time as another drawing app that uses WinTab, pressure may not arrive.

docs.h: Pen pressure is wrong or doesn't work
docs.x: You have to press hard to get thickness, or even a light touch is thick: Calibrate again to your touch with "Calibrate with test strokes". To adjust by hand, if you have to press hard to get thickness, lower the max; if even a light touch is thick, move the response toward "Firm". Light strokes are almost invisible, or the taper is too thin: Under Pen & input → Stroke feel, set "How tapering is made" to "Taper by length". Parts with weak pressure then never get thinner than 1px. It works with other brushes, but the thickness doesn't change for one brush: In that sub tool's tool properties, check that "Pen pressure to size" isn't turned off (Detailed brush settings). The thickness doesn't change when you draw with a mouse: A mouse has no pressure. For a mouse, the taper is always made from the "Taper start" and "Taper end" lengths of the sub tool. "The pen tablet driver has no free WinTab slots" appears and "Read pen pressure directly (WinTab)" turns off: Close other drawing apps that use WinTab, or restart your pen tablet driver (or the PC), and then turn it on again. With some drivers, the slot used by an app that quit without closing properly doesn't come back until you restart. "WinTab not found" or "Pen tablet not found" appears: Check that the pen tablet driver is installed and that the tablet is connected. You turned on WinTab, but "Current pressure" stays at "— (no pressure)" when you press the pad: With the PetaNuri3D window in front, press and draw on the pad with the pen a few times (if nothing arrives, it tries switching the connection method every two presses). If it still doesn't work, click "Search again" under "WinTab connection", and draw again. The pen doesn't respond after you turn WinTab on: Click "Search again" under "WinTab connection" in "Tablet", and draw again. It forgets the connection method it remembered and searches from scratch. You have per-app settings in your pen tablet driver: If you have added PetaNuri3D (PetaNuri3D-win_x64.exe) to the per-app settings, check there that pressure isn't turned off. "WinTab is running, but no pen data is arriving" appears: Use "Check WinTab status" below to find out where it is stopping. You want to reinstall or update the pen tablet driver: Close PetaNuri3D first. While WinTab is in use, the driver's files stay open. Lines appear late behind the pen tip: Try turning on "Show pen strokes early (reduce lag)" under Pen & input → Reduce lag (when drawing with the pen via Windows Ink). Also turn on "Predicted preview line" (Pen & input settings).
